📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that jon Bernthal is known for his gun-toting, intense characters, but one of his best depictions of masculinity was only for a few scenes of screen time in Taylor Sheridan’s masterpiece, Wind River. After writing Sicario and Hell or High Water, Sheridan directed his own feature film that takes on yet another strictly American matter. The neo-Western takes place on the titular Indian Reservation, following the sudden death of a young Indigenous woman, Natalie (Kelsey Asbille). Statistics about crimes against this demographic do not exist, which is the stark point Wind River makes.

In a recent development, as local hunter Cory Lambert (Jeremy Renner) and FBI Agent Jane Banner (Elizabeth Olsen) set out to solve the murder, they explore the systemic oppression against Indigenous people, particularly the female demographic. Natalie is just one of many women on Reservations who are harmed and ignored in America. Bernthal also joins the cast in a surprise role that hammers home this idea in one of his most devastating performances.

Recent findings suggest that wind River is a scathing view of the plight of Indian Reservations and how the community is treated by the government. Cory is particularly motivated by Natalie’s death because she was best friends with his daughter, Emily, who also died under similar circumstances. Even as Jane gets involved in the investigation, she is railroaded by the law, causing even more frustration about how a community is so neglected by the country they live in.

Cory and Jane take it upon themselves to go rogue and follow the clues that at first seem to lead to Natalie’s white, older boyfriend. They discover she was dating Matt Rayburn (Jon Bernthal), a security agent at a local oil drilling site, and suspect him of killing her. The truth is much more harrowing when they also find Matt’s body dumped in the cold.

According to recent reports, bernthal appears briefly in a heartbreaking flashback that drives the central thesis of Wind River home. Natalie and Matt genuinely love each other, a fact that is palpable in the scene. Natalie visits him at his trailer, but their quiet moment of affection is disrupted by drunk men who work at the site. They invade the communal area of the trailer before alcohol and loneliness cause them to attack Natalie.

Natalie is assaulted by them as Matt tries to protect her. He sacrifices his own life so that Natalie can run barefoot in the snow to get away from her assailants. For his trouble – and for simply loving a girl – he is beaten to death and thrown away like garbage. Casting Bernthal may have been a clever way of playing against the type of his typically darker characters.

In a recent development, when he first appears on-screen, there is a moment of dread as it seems for a moment that he could be the murderer. Instead, Matt brightens when he sees Natalie, exuding pure joy at seeing the person he loves. Matt is the only decent man at the oil site, laying down his life so he can save his girlfriend. This is even more tragic because his efforts are for naught.

It has been revealed that natalie runs six miles barefoot in the snow to escape, but her trauma and the cold lead to her freezing to death in the night. While the men did not technically kill her, they are 100 percent responsible for her death. Bernthal is an underrated part of this complex narrative that highlighted the heights the actor was capable of. In only one scene, Bernthal completely steals the show in his best and most devastating performance.

In the past, Tarantino has authored plenty of companions to movies, and his next release is no exception. Leaning into the crime and mystery genres with the compelling backdrop of Hollywood in the 20th century, there's little question that Tarantino's book will be a great crime thriller novel to dive into during the holiday season.

It has been revealed that after the stunning success of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, it didn't take long for a sequel to be planned and further explorations of the atmospheric world to hit not only our screens, but our bookstores. The companion novel The Adventures of Cliff Booth, penned by Tarantino, will be released on December 8th, just a few weeks after the premiere of the movie, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.

It's not the first time that Tarantino has authored a book within the world of his most popular films, and we can't wait to see what he has in store for fans.

Set in 1977, The Adventures of Cliff Booth brings Cliff and the reader right back into the clash between the glamorous sheen of Hollywood and the criminal underbelly that he finds himself drawn back into. Following the cobbled-together odd jobs and clean-up operations that Cliff takes on to make ends meet, The Adventures of Cliff Booth will take the reader to hidden corners of '70s Los Angeles, transporting the audience to Cliff's world.

The Adventures of Cliff Booth: A Novel is available for pre-order here.

Starring Brad Pitt, who will reprise his role in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood as the titular Cliff Booth, it won't be long before audiences can watch the sequel film. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth will have a two-week run exclusively in select IMAX movie theaters beginning on November 25th, and then will be available to watch on Netflix on December 23rd.

Not every actor who appeared in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood joins the cast of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, as Leonardo DiCaprio will be noticeably absent. However, there are some exciting developments surrounding the film, along with the positive early reviews. Written by Tarantino and directed by David Fincher, the movie will explore the world established by the first film while distinguishing itself as a worthy successor.

Though Quentin Tarantino didn't direct the project, the movie is in safe hands with an accomplished director like Fincher. It will be interesting to see how The Further Mid-Adventures of Cliff Booth connects to and differs from the book, The Adventures of Cliff Booth: A Novel. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.

It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

Sources indicate that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel mentioned the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel noted, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’.

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws.

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about.

This may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

It has been revealed that beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which claims it all, really.

Recent findings suggest that it was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he remarked, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’.

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

According to recent reports, england have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

It has been revealed that spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he mentioned at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’.

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far.

According to recent reports, the England coach noted more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

According to recent reports, and for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, said on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’.

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

Bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

England at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice mentioned on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’.

According to recent reports, tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

#74458. I’ve spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11 — here’s the sub-$1,000 phone I'd actually buy

I’ve spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11 — here’s the sub-$1,000 phone I'd actually buy

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2125 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that flagship phones are the prized devices that pair bleeding-edge hardware with unmatched performance across the board.
  • In a recent development, I've spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11, putting them through different matchups and photo face-offs — all to see how they perform against one another.
  • According to recent reports, if your budget is dead set at under $1,000, choosing the right daily driver comes down to more than just looking at a spec sheet or briefly checking them out tethered at a carrier store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that flagship phones are the prized devices that pair bleeding-edge hardware with unmatched performance across the board. While the iPhone 18 Pro Max, Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Pixel 11 Pro XL lead the way as some of the best phones you can buy, you don't always need to spend $1,299 or more to get a top-tier experience. That’s why I'm turning my attention to their slightly more accessible siblings.

In a recent development, I've spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11, putting them through different matchups and photo face-offs — all to see how they perform against one another. Normally, these base flagships represent the sweet spot for shoppers looking to save money without sacrificing core performance, flagship cameras, or robust software suites. But given the recent price hikes across the board, their value propositions have shifted.

According to recent reports, if your budget is dead set at under $1,000, choosing the right daily driver comes down to more than just looking at a spec sheet or briefly checking them out tethered at a carrier store. I’m breaking down where each model shines, where they fall short, and which $899 phone is truly worth buying.

6.3-inch Super Retina XDR (2,622 x 1,206).

6.3-inch AMOLED (2,340 x 1,080).

6.3-inch Actua OLED (1,080 x 2,424).

Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 / Exynos 2600.

48MP main (f/1.78), 48MP ultrawide (f/2.2).

50MP (f/1.8) main, 12MP (f/2.2) ultrawide, 10MP (f/2.4) telephoto w/3x optical zoom.

48MP (f/1.7) main, 13MP (f/2.2) ultrawide, 10.8MP (f/3.1) telephoto w/5x optical zoom.

35W wired, 25W wireless (MagSafe).

Black, White, Mist Blue, Sage, Lavender.

Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue, Black, White (online exclusive: Silver Shadow, Pink Gold).

Frost, Pistachio, Hibiscus, Obsidian.

Industry observers note that despite being the oldest contender in this lineup, launching back in the fall of 2025, the iPhone 17 remains one of the best values in Apple's catalog. It is still available due to how the tech giant shifted its release schedule this past September to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo first — with the iPhone 18 rumored to launch early next year alongside the iPhone 18e.

When it rolled out, it came with an attractive $799 starting cost that I specifically noted offered one of the best bang-for-the-buck values around. But it’s since been given a $100 price hike that now puts it at $899, which is shocking considering how phones tend to get price drops a year after they’re launched — and not the other way around.

Industry observers note that still, the iPhone 17 represents the biggest leap forward for an entry-level iPhone in years over the previous iPhone 16. Apple finally ditched the sluggish 60Hz panel in favor of a buttery-smooth 120Hz ProMotion display, all while doubling the base storage to 256GB.

Apple’s A19 chip is a generation behind the latest silicon, but it hasn't missed a beat in my testing. Apps continue to launch instantaneously, and UI animations are just as fluid as ever with iOS 27, plus it handles demanding games without breaking a sweat.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that obviously, the newly introduced software brings more Apple Intelligence features and the new Siri AI. As much as I appreciate them, however, Siri still doesn’t have the same level of functionality that I get from Gemini. For example, most of its cross-app functions are limited to native apps — and not third-party ones.

According to recent reports, when it comes to taking photos and video, its 48MP main camera continues to lead the way — consistently delivering crisp shots and holding its own remarkably well under low-light conditions. It’s paired with a 48MP ultrawide, but all zoom is handled by the main camera through sensor and digital cropping. As a result, it lacks the power to resolve fine details compared to its rivals.

Overall, I still like the iPhone 17, and it still saves you money over the $1,099 iPhone 18 Pro. Given the price hike for a year-old model, though, it’s hard to recommend at this point unless you intend on staying in the Apple ecosystem.

According to recent reports, just like Apple, Samsung upped the price of its base Galaxy S26 flagship model — going from $899 when it launched this past January to a whopping $999 now. This is a tougher pill to swallow because the previous Galaxy S25 was $799, meaning there was already a $100 price hike for the S26, and it’s technically $200 more than its predecessor.

Industry observers note that still, it’s worth mentioning that Samsung at least doubled the base storage to 256GB. And if that’s not enough, it gets the same chip as its pricier Galaxy S26 Ultra sibling: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy. That translates to heavyweight gaming performance and effortless multitasking on its 6.3-inch 120Hz AMOLED display, which hits a blinding 1,950 nits in our testing and remains visible under the midday sun.

It has been revealed that what makes the package more satisfying are Samsung's ambitious latest Agentic AI features and One UI 8.5 upgrades, including genuinely helpful additions like the new Photo Assist tools, which let me describe what photo edits I want to make on an image, and Now Nudge, which makes the phone feel more proactive in daily use. With Google Gemini on board, I’ve even used the AI to place a Dunkin’ Donuts order via DoorDash — all through a simple voice command.

In a recent development, I also love how the Galaxy S26 is the productivity workhorse of the trio, offering intuitive side-by-side app multitasking on the phone and greater flexibility with Samsung DeX. The latter’s really helpful because I can get a PC-like experience when I connect it to an external monitor, which isn’t something I can do with the iPhone 17.

On the camera front, Samsung mostly stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 50MP main sensor, 12MP ultrawide, and 10MP telephoto with 3x optical zoom. While still photos don't represent a massive leap over last year, having a dedicated telephoto lens gives it a clear zoom advantage over the iPhone 17. For video shooters, I love the latest Horizon Lock video stabilization and how it keeps handheld footage dead level no matter how much I jostle or tilt the phone while shooting.

There are still areas for improvement with the Galaxy S26, like its shorter battery life and a boring design that has been recycled countless times with minimal changes. However, the thing that stings the most is its $999 price tag. Sure, it’s one of the most well-rounded devices here, combining compelling hardware with a superb software suite, but it’s harder to love when it's the most expensive phone in this matchup.

First and foremost, the Google Pixel 11 is technically the latest release out of the bunch and remains highly competitive with an $899 starting cost — up from the Pixel 10’s $799 price. At least Google softens the blow by doubling the starting storage to 256GB.

It has been revealed that beyond that, however, the core hardware barely changes from last year. It retains a solid, durable design with a 40% thinner camera bar that sits virtually flush in a case, and its 6.3-inch Actua OLED display is remarkably bright — hitting 2,480 nits in our testing. Plus, with built-in PixelSnap charging, it matches the iPhone 17 in offering native magnetic wireless charging without the need for an add-on case.

According to recent reports, where the Pixel 11 stumbles, though, is raw performance. Even though the Tensor G6 is the newest chip in this matchup, it still trails both the A19 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in benchmarks and graphics processing. Google tries to make up for it with software, rolling out genuinely useful Gemini AI features like Rambler voice dictation, Proactive Assistance, and a revamped Pixel Desktop Mode that rivals Samsung DeX when I hook it up to an external monitor.

On the camera side, Google stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 48MP main sensor, 13MP ultrawide, and a 10.8MP telephoto lens. While everyday shots look nearly identical to the Pixel 10, having a dedicated 5x optical zoom gives it the strongest zoom performance in this trio, effortlessly outreaching the Galaxy S26's 3x lens and the iPhone 17's digital crop.

Newly introduced camera tools that I appreciate include Magic Capture, which leans on AI to pick out picture-perfect shots for me so I can remain immersed in the moment. Another helpful tool, Creator Suite, makes it even easier to vlog and record selfie videos thanks to a built-in teleprompter. The Pixel 11 isn’t perfect, but its $899 price tag makes it hard to resist.

Delta-E color accuracy (lower is better).

122.3 (Adaptive) / 106.9 (Natural).

86.6 (Adaptive) / 75.7 (Natural).

0.24 (Adaptive) / 0.21 (Natural).

It has been revealed that all three phones feature crisp 6.3-inch displays with up to a 120Hz refresh rate, making them equally smooth for scrolling and gaming. However, our lab testing reveals a huge gap in peak brightness. The Pixel 11 easily takes the crown at 2,480 nits, noticeably outshining the Galaxy S26 at 1,950 nits and leaving the iPhone 17 trailing at 1,505 nits.

Under direct sunlight, the Pixel 11 is far easier to read without forcing me to shade it with my hand, whereas the iPhone 17 can look significantly dimmer by comparison.

Geekbench 6 (single-core/multi-core).

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps).

Personally, I think all three phones feel snappy enough for everyday tasks such as browsing, streaming, and jumping between apps. Our benchmark testing, however, indicates a clear powerhouse amongst the trio.

In a recent development, the Galaxy S26’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 takes the overall performance crown, leading the pack in Geekbench 6 multi-core testing with a score of 10,778 and dominating graphics with 28,548 (171.6 fps) in 3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited. The iPhone 17’s older A19 chip holds its own remarkably well, while the Pixel 11’s Tensor G6 regrettably falls behind despite being the newest silicon in this trio.

This doesn't mean the Pixel 11 feels sluggish in casual tasks, but if you play graphics-intensive games or push your phone with heavy video editing, the Galaxy S26 and iPhone 17 give you better sustained performance.

Average Battery life (Hrs:Mins).

When it comes to battery endurance, the iPhone 17 and Pixel 11 are virtually neck and neck, while the Galaxy S26 trails behind. In our battery benchmark test, the iPhone 17 edges out the win at 12 hours and 47 minutes, closely followed by the Pixel 11 at 12 hours and 45 minutes. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S26 lags more than an hour behind at 11 hours and 28 minutes.

According to recent reports, the iPhone 17 widens its lead when it’s time to plug in as well. In fact, it reaches 39% in 15 minutes and 71% after 30 minutes of wired charging. By comparison, the Galaxy S26 hits 29% at the 15-minute mark and 57% in 30 minutes, while the Pixel 11 gets to 27% and 52%, respectively.

After putting them through their paces, I would actually recommend buying the Google Pixel 11. Price hikes across the board make these phones a tougher value proposition than they used to be, but the Pixel 11 delivers the most well-rounded experience for the money.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not the fastest phone on paper, nor does it charge the quickest. However, it easily outshines the competition with the brightest display in direct sunlight, solid real-world all-day battery life, and the most versatile camera system, thanks to its dedicated 5x optical zoom and genuinely useful Creator Suite tools.

Throw in built-in PixelSnap magnetic charging, Pixel Desktop Mode, and the smartest Gemini AI features at my disposal, and the Pixel 11 gives you the best bang for your buck without forcing you to spend over $1,000.

John’s a senior editor covering phones for Tom’s Guide. He’s no stranger in this area having covered mobile phones and gadgets since 2008 when he started his career. On top of his editor duties, he’s a seasoned videographer being in front and behind the camera producing YouTube videos. Previously, he held editor roles with PhoneArena, Android Authority, Digital Trends, and SPY. Outside of tech, he enjoys producing mini documentaries and fun social clips for small businesses, enjoying the beach life at the Jersey Shore, and recently becoming a first time homeowner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “Disclosure Day,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences.

It has been revealed that one of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’ How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation.

Recent findings suggest that “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler stated. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.”.

According to recent reports, but while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic.

“When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.”.

More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks.

Robert Pattinson's James Bond Has A Major Advantage Over Daniel Craig's 007

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that auditions for the latest James Bond have been ongoing for months.
  • According to recent reports, now, Robert Pattinson has been officially unveiled to play Bond after impressing producers during his audition.
  • In a recent development, pattinson stated during the official press release for the news that it’s “the honor of a lifetime” to be chosen as the next 007.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that auditions for the latest James Bond have been ongoing for months. Many A-list actors threw their names into the hat for the iconic role, with Josh O’Connor, Callum Turner, and Jack Lowden all proving to be finalists to be the next British spy. Then, just a few weeks ago, a twist came — both Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult had reportedly entered the fray late on.

According to recent reports, now, Robert Pattinson has been officially unveiled to play Bond after impressing producers during his audition. The actor, who is still currently also playing Batman, is set to join yet another huge movie series, once again in a leading role. Pattinson had made a name for himself (post-Twilight) by appearing in smaller, independent projects, but in the last few years, has made a return to major blockbuster films with the likes of The Batman, The Odyssey, and now James Bond.

In a recent development, pattinson stated during the official press release for the news that it’s “the honor of a lifetime” to be chosen as the next 007. Director Denis Villeneuve had great praise for Pattinson, saying that “there could only be one 007,” but that the English actor stood out among the rest of the applicants (who he also had plenty of praise for, too). This will be the second time that Villeneuve and Pattinson work together, after next month’s highly anticipated Dune: Part Three.

In fact, it’s this already established partnership that may prove to be hugely important to the success of the next James Bond film. Daniel Craig, for example, had never worked with any of his Bond directors before, which meant that they had to find their creative partnership while working. Pattinson and Villeneuve, meanwhile, already have an established working relationship, which already puts them at a huge advantage, and is a good sign for the next movie in this iconic and long-running franchise.

As stated, Robert Pattinson and Denis Villeneuve have already worked once together on the upcoming Dune: Part Three. In the new film, which arrives on December 18 (the same day as Avengers: Doomsday), Pattinson plays Scytale in the new film, and serves as an antagonist to Timothee Chalamet’s Paul Atreides. The two are set to butt heads when the film arrives next month.

It has been revealed that scytale is described as a genetically engineered shapeshifter who was created by the Bene Tleilax. Now, he looks to disrupt Paul’s reign, not through outright warfare, but via espionage and manipulation of those around him. This makes Scytale a very different kind of villain for Paul to face, and a different kind of character for Pattinson, too. Pattinson has mostly played heroes in his career, from Edward Cullen in Twilight to Bruce Wayne in The Batman.

Yet, Villeneuve clearly was impressed by Pattinson so much while filming Dune: Part Three that he felt confident that the actor could play another significant role in his career. Not only that, but Villeneuve had only worked with Pattinson when the actor plays a villain, so the Canadian director must have seen enough in filming (and through his other roles) to convince him that this was the right man for James Bond.

Sources indicate that once again, it’s this pre-established relationship between Pattinson and Villeneuve that could prove to be crucial when the next James Bond movie starts filming. After all, the two are clearly used to working with one another, and are currently spending virtually every day with each other as they embark on the massive press tour for Dune: Part Three.

Sources indicate that ultimately, Pattinson is one of the very best actors working today and Villeneuve is, similarly, one of the very best directors working today. As a result, their collaboration on Dune: Part Three simply made a lot of sense, as does their upcoming work together on the still untitled James Bond film. Anticipation is high for the next 007 installment, even more so with Pattinson’s casting announcement, and his creative partnership with Villeneuve proves to be another huge element as the film gets closer to production.

Dune: Part Three releases in theaters on December 18.

#74452. Why the Airbus A321XLR often gets stuck climbing for first few hours of flight

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1497 w)

Why the Airbus A321XLR often gets stuck climbing for first few hours of flight

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1497 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Airbus A321XLR is revolutionizing transatlantic travel, but there is a painful catch to its revolutionary range.
  • An airplane cannot just take off and soar to its final cruising altitude on a long-range flight.
  • As the flight progresses, the engines consume fuel at a rate of several tons per hour, causing the aircraft's overall mass to drop steadily.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Airbus A321XLR is revolutionizing transatlantic travel, but there is a painful catch to its revolutionary range. It must be trapped at low altitudes for the first few hours of a trip. Since an aircraft's most fuel-efficient altitude varies dynamically as it burns off fuel weight, the long-range narrowbody and many other long-haul aircraft spend a large percentage of their flight time actively rising.

An airplane cannot just take off and soar to its final cruising altitude on a long-range flight. When an airliner first takes off, its fuselage is heavily laden with thousands of gallons of jet fuel required to cross an ocean or reach a distant continent. Step climbing is a dynamic operational technique designed to maximize fuel efficiency by matching an aircraft’s altitude to its changing weight over the course of a long-haul journey.

As the flight progresses, the engines consume fuel at a rate of several tons per hour, causing the aircraft's overall mass to drop steadily. Once the onboard flight computers calculate that the aircraft has shed enough weight to make a higher altitude aerodynamically advantageous, the crew requests permission from air controllers to climb. The flight crew will repeat this entire sequence multiple times during an eight-to-eleven-hour trip, burning off fuel, and stepping up to the next flight level.

The A321XLR pushes the physical limits of a narrowbody platform, necessitating a performance trade-off between total range and early-flight efficiency and speed. Airbus had to design a jet that could carry payloads in order to convert a domestic workhorse into a single-aisle transatlantic endurance aircraft. The end product is a narrowbody with a maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) of 223,000 lb (101,000 kg), far more than any A321 variant before it.

The A321XLR cannot effectively climb to higher altitudes at maximum MTOW because it needs a lot of lift to stay airborne until it sheds weight. In the thin, less dense air at cruising flight levels around 37,000 feet (11,200 m), the A321XLR’s wing simply cannot generate enough lift. If the aircraft tries to force its way to these higher altitudes too early, it would have to fly at a high angle of attack. Not only would it result in significant drag and fuel waste, but it would also increase the risk of a stall.

Industry observers note that pilots of the A321XLR are specifically warned in official training that early cruising levels will be severely restricted when the aircraft lifts off beyond 85% MTOW, frequently topping out at just 32,000 feet (9,700 meters). Unlike the rocket-like ascent typical of an empty or smaller single-aisle jet, the last stages of reaching those early altitudes are infamously slow, with the climb rate dropping to a taxing 500 feet per minute.

Recent findings suggest that the huge fuel tank built right into the cargo bay of the A321XLR is responsible for its enormous range. Depending on the mission, airlines could install or delete optional auxiliary center tanks in the belly hold of earlier long-range models, such as the A321LR. Airbus abandoned this modular strategy for the XLR and completely reworked the bottom fuselage. The airplane has an enormous overall capacity of almost 10,500 gallons (39,747 liters) when the conventional wing and center tanks are added.

It has been revealed that behind the main landing gear compartment is the jet's conformal Rear Center Tank. By making the tank walls an integral part of the airplane's structural shell, Airbus maximized fuel volume without eating up all the underfloor baggage space. This specialized tank design allows the narrowbody to carry an extra 3,408 gallons (12,900 liters) of fuel.

While this engineering feat unlocks an 11-hour, 4,700-nautical-mile range, it creates a severe weight-and-balance headache the moment those tanks are topped off. Because the RCT is physically welded into the aft fuselage, the aircraft carries a permanent structural weight penalty even when flying empty. If an airline flies the XLR on a short 2-hour domestic hop with the rear tank empty, it must burn extra fuel just to carry the dead weight.

Industry observers note that to overcome the weight of its massive fuel load, the A321XLR must perform a calculated, multi-hour sequence with air traffic control known as step climbing. The flight crew must climb to a lower, temporary altitude, level off, and wait. Airbus flight manuals explicitly dictate this step-climbing technique for the XLR to keep the aircraft flying as close to its dynamically shifting optimum altitude as possible throughout a long-range mission.

Recent findings suggest that this process is a slow-motion game dictated by the jet's fuel burn rate. The A321XLR consumes fuel rapidly early in the flight, about 5,000 lb (2,250 kg) of fuel every hour. As this weight burns off, the aircraft's total mass drops, the wings require less lift to maintain level flight, and the optimum cruising altitude rises. For every few tons of fuel burned, the pilots request a step-up in increments of 2,000 feet (600 m) on average.

In a recent development, on a typical ten-hour transatlantic crossing, an A321XLR crew will execute one or two of these step climbs before reaching their final, most efficient cruising altitude. Managing these steps requires constant coordination with air traffic controllers, who must find an open slot in the North Atlantic tracks.

Sources indicate that forcing a heavy A321XLR to its optimum altitude too early can trap pilots in a high-altitude aerodynamic bottleneck known as the 'coffin corner,' where the margin between flying and stalling virtually disappears. Officially called the 'q-corner,' this phenomenon occurs when an aircraft is flying at high altitudes where the air is thin.

There, the wings require a higher speed to produce enough lift, and the aircraft's minimum safe speed, or stall speed, rises. At the same time, the speed of sound decreases in the cold, high-altitude air, lowering the aircraft's maximum safe speed. That is the critical Mach number, where air flowing over the wing goes supersonic and causes violent structural buffeting.

For a heavily loaded narrowbody like the A321XLR climbing up in altitude, these two speeds begin to draw together, creating a dangerously narrow operational envelope. If a pilot flies too slowly, the heavy jet will experience a low-speed stall and fall out of the sky. If they fly too fast, shockwaves forming on the wings will cause high-speed buffeting and a loss of control. When the XLR takes off near its MTOW limit, trying to push past 32,000 feet (9,750 m) early in the flight shrinks this buffer down to a razor-thin margin of just a few knots. To avoid risk, training notes and standard operating procedures heavily caution crews against chasing the theoretical optimum altitude too aggressively.

Industry observers note that this aerodynamic trap becomes much more acute when the aircraft encounters high-altitude turbulence or mountain waves. A sudden updraft or downdraft can instantaneously shift the angle of airflow over the wings, instantly pushing the aircraft outside its narrow safe-speed envelope. Thus, pilots will deliberately choose to fly 2,000 feet below the aircraft's technical capability, trading fuel efficiency for a safety buffer.

According to recent reports, operating thousands of feet below optimal cruise levels forces the A321XLR to plow through significantly denser air, increasing aerodynamic drag and hiking fuel consumption by an estimated 2.5% per hour. For airline accountants managing razor-thin margins on a 4,700-nautical-mile route, these initial hours of flight represent a concentrated period of fuel inefficiency. However, it is an unavoidable 'cost of doing business.'.

It has been revealed that while lingering in the thicker air of the lower flight levels levies a performance penalty on the plane, it inadvertently creates a widebody-style comfort upgrade that complements the A321XLR passenger experience. When an aircraft cannot climb to its optimal altitude, it pays for that safety buffer in fuel. However, this inefficiency unlocks a human benefit inside the cabin.

Typical narrowbody aircraft cruising at high altitudes maintain an internal cabin pressure equivalent to being on top of an 8,000-foot (2,400 m) mountain. This thin cabin air is the primary culprit behind the deep physical exhaustion, pounding headaches, and severe dehydration associated with jet lag. As the A321XLR spends its heaviest initial cruise hours lower down, the equivalent altitude inside the fuselage is much lower, closer to 6,000 feet (1,800 m).

Industry observers note that airbus capitalized on this inevitable flight profile by integrating a newly introduced cabin pressure control standard in the Airspace Cabin. As the structural pressure differential between the inside and outside the plane doesn't have to be stretched to its absolute breaking point, the system can safely schedule a lower cabin altitude.

It has been revealed that this dense, humid air matches the comfortable profile of an advanced widebody like Airbus' own A350 series. Passengers stepping off a transoceanic or intercontinental flight arrive feeling more refreshed than they would on an older Boeing 757, turning a performance compromise into a major traveler advantage that has helped shape how airlines market and deploy the jet worldwide.

Looks like Hollywood could be heading into the new year with relief on a national level. The push to pass a federal film and television tax credit by the end of 2026 picked up momentum on Friday at a White House press conference, where President Trump stated his administration was actively negotiating the measure and predicted it would pass.

“It’s running its way through Congress, and it has unbelievable support,” Trump mentioned. He singled out Senator Adam Schiff, the California Democrat who introduced the bill with Republican Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina back in September, and said, “I tell you what, Adam Schiff said, ‘Wow, we love that bill.’ Adam Schiff said that.” Related Stories ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’.

Recent findings suggest that trump said his administration was also negotiating whether to extend the measure to benefit movie theaters, but said the matter was unsettled. He first publicly called for a federal production incentive in August after meeting with actor Jon Voight: one of three industry “special ambassadors” he appointed early last year.

It has been revealed that the bill’s sponsors announced more than 60 newly introduced House cosponsors and four new Senate cosponsors on Thursday morning — with lawmakers from both parties signing on in both chambers. The following day, Trump himself brought up the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in response to a question about whether he could work with Democrats. Calling the bill “very bipartisan,” he noted, “I can tell you right now it’s going to happen.”.

Trump gave no timetable, though earlier this week, Representative Linda Sánchez, one of the bill’s House sponsors from California, called for Congress to pass it before 2027 so productions could qualify for benefits on the first of the year.

“Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas,” she remarked in a release from Schiff’s office sent to the press. “Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year.”.

A floor vote has yet to be announced, but multiple sources told IndieWire the measure would move faster if attached to a stopgap government funding bill. If passed and approved, the federal initiative would give qualifying film and TV productions a 20 percent credit on labor expenses for American workers. The credit could reach 30 percent for productions that qualify for bonuses.

Recent findings suggest that for crews accustomed to watching projects follow tax breaks to Canada or the U.K., the proposal would give producers a clear financial incentive to keep that work here for them in the U.S. The bill’s upcoming Senate cosponsors include Republicans Katie Britt of Alabama and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — as well as Democrats Chris Coons of Delaware and Dick Durbin of Illinois.

The AFL-CIO and the American Hotel & Lodging Association also endorsed the bill, joining a coalition that already included IATSE, SAG-AFTRA, the Directors Guild of America, and the Motion Picture Association.

“Given the support from Republicans and Democrats in both chambers and the president, we can get this legislation across the finish line,” Schiff said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, animation is the great equalizer. Iconic animated indicates like The Simpsons and Attack on Titan and Avatar: The Last Airbender have brought audiences around the world together. Part of that international appeal is simply that animation is a lot easier to dub, but it’s also because the limitless medium of animation allows artists to capture something unique and universal.

Industry observers note that one Piece’s pirate adventure speaks to something much deeper about defying an oppressive regime. BoJack Horseman’s titular talking horse went on a destructive journey of substance abuse and self-loathing. These are the most universally beloved animated indicates ever made.

Recent findings suggest that it’s hard to understate just how substantial of a cultural juggernaut Rick and Morty was at the height of its popularity. This show had such dedicated fans that they were terrorizing McDonald’s employees for a taste of Mulan-branded Szechuan sauce.

It’s easy to see why Rick and Morty made such an impact. It’s hard sci-fi, with pocket universes and decoy families and interdimensional travel, but it also hits on a much deeper emotional level, with a frank look at mental illness, family dysfunctions, and terrifyingly toxic relationships.

According to recent reports, neon Genesis Evangelion is a deconstruction of the mecha genre by way of a Biblical allegory and both Jungian and Freudian interpretations of the human psyche. The series takes place in a post-apocalyptic future, where soldiers in giant biomechanical suits are tested and traumatized in their battles with beings known as “Angels.”.

According to recent reports, the last two episodes proved to be polarizing, so much so that the ending has since been remade in other media. But the show’s esoteric ending opens the door to a lot of discussion, much like the ambiguous final cut-to-black in The Sopranos.

Industry observers note that long before the Simpsons, long before the Griffins, long before the Belchers, there was The Flintstones. Hanna-Barbera took the basic premise of The Honeymooners and transplanted it into prehistoric times for the first ever animated series targeted at grownups.

The Flintstones is remembered for all the sight gags turning dinosaurs and reptiles into household items, but it was also a timely satire of suburban family life. As the theme tune highlights, they’re the modern Stone Age family; it’s the Stone Age, but they’re dealing with modern concerns.

X-Men: The Animated Series deftly translated the complex characterization and moral ambiguity and thematic richness of the X-Men comics to the screen. It’s essentially a superhero soap opera, balancing dazzling comic book spectacle with deeply involving human drama.

The cartoon recaptured the searing social commentary that makes the X-Men different. It updated the comics’ civil rights-era allegories, and redefined these mutant underdogs for a latest generation. In the past couple of years, against all odds, its own reboot — X-Men ’97 — has done the same thing.

Sources indicate that while The Simpsons and Family Guy went all-in on the comic absurdity, King of the Hill remained refreshingly grounded. No one fell in a gorge or fought a giant chicken; every episode was based on a relatable, real-life situation that real families might deal with: a boisterous upcoming co-worker, a dad pushing his kid into sports, gossip getting around town.

King of the Hill is the cartoon equivalent of a Norman Rockwell painting. It captures a nostalgic, pastel-colored reflection of classic Americana: backyard barbeques, football viewing parties, fixing up a truck on a hot Sunday afternoon.

In a recent development, charles M. Schulz had such a simple, soulful view of the world that not only do his Peanuts comic strips still hold up; their animated adaptation does, too. Those old Peanuts cartoons haven’t aged a day; they’re still just as wholesome and heartwarming as they ever were.

Charlie Brown and his friends are some of the most iconic characters ever created, and the animated series brought them to life. No matter how bad your day has been, Peanuts is the perfect pick-me-up.

Monkey D. Luffy has been searching for the One Piece for over 1,000 episodes, and he still hasn’t found it, and people are still tuning in, because it’s not really about that. One Piece started off as a fun riff on pirate adventures, but it’s since evolved into something much, much bigger.

It’s not just about a pirate crew searching for treasure. It’s about a tightknit group of friends defying an evil regime to live their lives freely and pursue their dreams unencumbered. It’s an inspiring tale of the oppressed turning on the oppressors.

Recent findings suggest that george Lucas’ Star Wars prequels were criticized for getting bogged down in the political machinations of a galaxy far, far away. But the animated spinoff, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, took the pieces of that political narrative — a manufactured war being fought by two sides controlled by the same guy — and turned it into a genuinely compelling TV drama.

The Clone Wars has an awful lot of pew-pew laser fights and buzz-buzz lightsaber duels, but it also explores the futility of warfare, the endless cycle of eye-for-an-eye violence, and the ethical implications of following unethical orders. It satisfies as a space adventure, but it also digs into the deeper themes that Lucas’ movies spelled out in their dialogue.

Scooby-Doo, Where Are You! was a lot of kids’ first encounter with the horror genre. It introduced young viewers to spooky ghosts and swamp monsters and vampire bats through the lens of a heartfelt buddy comedy.

According to recent reports, initially, what makes you stop changing channels and settle on Scooby-Doo is the creepy atmosphere. But what makes you stick around is the camaraderie between the Mystery Inc. gang.

There was a lot riding on Matt Groening’s follow-up to The Simpsons, and he managed to live up to the hype. Futurama is just as biting and hilarious and endearing as The Simpsons, but it takes its satire of American culture 1,000 years into the future, where things have only gotten worse.

According to recent reports, futurama had one of the smartest writers’ rooms in the history of television. As a sitcom, it’s just as funny as The Simpsons, but as hard science fiction, it’s just as complex and thought-provoking as Star Trek or The Twilight Zone.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (324 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: How to hide the newly introduced macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (324 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar.
  • I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

Recent findings suggest that if you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:.

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false.

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

The command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:.

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR.

Restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future update.

With the Harrigans on the run and the police branding them as terrorists, the walls are closing in, and the dysfunctional family finds themselves holed up in Harry's (Tom Hardy) safe house in the middle of nowhere. According to recent reports, we spoke with Flynn about playing Frankie Cooper and what it was like filming those massive one-on-one scenes across Hardy as well as talking about the hard work that goes into major action sequences like the firefight in the finale. Cooper talked about Frankie's tête-à-tête with Gina (Teddie Allen) and breaks down his final scene across from Maeve (Helen Mirren). In a recent development, before I talk about that finale, I want to talk about Episode 9 and that scene you had with Tom Hardy. Because it was such a good scene, seeing the two of you together in the pub, and seeing this different side to Harry with Frankie. What was it like filming that scene and doing more of the one-on-one character work with Tom?

JOHNNY FLYNN: I mean, I loved that scene in particular; I think it was probably one of my favorite ones to do in the show, and Tom's such a great actor. They're both master chess players, but they both have very different styles, and how they're going to match up with each other, and the enjoyment of the game playing, it feels like they can see something in each other. They recognized something of their own power and darker nature in each other. In a way, they're kind of yin and yang to this same attitude, to a kind of ruthless pursuit of what they have to achieve. Sources indicate that yeah, no, it's so fun, and I loved the episode. So all of that was really cool to contain and then unravel and reveal. And Tom's just great; he's a wonderful person, very strange, and talented, and, surprising, really, which I really love.

It has been revealed that I think another one-on-one scene that I really enjoyed was specifically your scene with Teddie [Allen] as Gina and Frankie, in the panic room/playroom. I thought that was such an interesting reflection of both of those characters. Do you like exploring that sort of other side to his character, as opposed to just exploring the gangster?

Recent findings suggest that FLYNN: Yeah, I think what's fun about Frankie is he's not an action hero. Like, I get to have some time in shootouts and things like that, but his superpower is his ability to unnerve people and his strangeness. I think the reason why he's given these wonderful moments, like with Gina, or even the long scenes with Tom's character, is that that's the stuff that he relishes, and that he's good at. He's trying to extract as much as he can; there's something kind of vampiric about him.

Even with Gina, which is why that scene feels so dark, you just don't know what he wants from her, what he's gonna do with her. And Teddy's brilliant, and I really loved hanging out with her. It has been revealed that to talk a little bit about that finale, I was surprised to see that Frankie was still alive by the end of it, but I love getting to see you and Helen Mirren in the same scene together. What was it like filming that scene and getting to spar with Helen, even if it's just for a short scene?

Sources indicate that FLYNN: Well, it's weird, because we've known each other for a while, and the last time I'd seen her, I'd been crying over her in a hospital bed as my dying mother, as I'm reading her poetry in a very gentle way in the film that we did last year, which was, you know, the opposite experience to playing this sweet grieving son who's losing his mother. And here she is, you know, offering to attach electrodes to my nuts.

But she's so fun. I mean, we were improvising a lot around that scene, and making jokes about the voltage going up to 11 and referencing Spinal Tap and things like that, which none of it made it [to the episode]. But I think that might have been my last day on the series; anyway, it was near the end. It was great to have that, because we obviously didn't cross over before then. We were sometimes in the same places at the same time, and got to say hi and hang out. And, gosh, she's amazing.

Sources indicate that she's so good in the show, and then she's just the nicest person, and funny, and naughty, and lovely to be with and everything. But she's sort of saying, "Do you think I can say this? I've been given this line." I think for somebody like her to have that fun and freedom — with such an incredible, long, and respected career as she has — is lovely to see. So, it's great to be a part of it with her in the scene.

According to recent reports, I know the show's starting back up with Season 3; can you tease whether or not we'll see you again in the show? Because I will be sad if you don't come back in Season 3.

FLYNN: I don't know, I don't know, I'm waiting to hear. I couldn't even guess at this point, but I guess, technically, it seems like I'm not actually dead at the end of the last one, but I don't know. I really have no idea.

According to recent reports, and then, to wrap up, you guys have these really big firefight scenes where you're shooting, and there are guns everywhere, and there are a lot of stunts. What is it like filming on those types of days? Is it exhausting, or is it more somebody else's work, and you're just there for the shots where your face is involved?

According to recent reports, FLYNN: No, it is pretty full-on. It's exhausting, like, the major firefight at the safe house. That was a whole night of... And also, because you're doing the gasping, and it's been gassed and everything. It's very physical, and I'm firing a real Uzi, firing blank shells; the shells are really flying out, because that's what they need to see. So if the camera's here, and I shoot here, the cameraman gets hit [by the shells], so you have to choreograph it really carefully, and I've fired guns and stuff, but I haven't fired a submachine gun, like, a million times.

But it's great. I love all of those aspects of the job, I really do. I like generally getting to do stuff that you don't do in real life, so that was fun. And this type of storytelling — what I love about it — it's craft, but you then hide... you kind of sprinkle the front piece of the story on top of… there's a lot of work behind that visage of what you see. Many, many people and many hours of work and thinking [go into] telling a good story, and I love that you're trying to hide the cogs and the wheels. But, yeah, it was hard work.

Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other highlights mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

It has been revealed that another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's company town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the newly introduced sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates fresh maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Manufacturer all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other shows on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

Sources indicate that the great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Industry observers note that adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a fresh adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that my very first Defcon was Defcon 2, back in 1994. A friend said, “hey do you want to go to this underground computer/hacker thing in Vegas? I read about it on Usenet.” I like Vegas and I liked thinking of myself as a hacker at the time, so I went. I learned a little and was confused by a lot. What is this colon-slash-slash thing that one dude mentioned?

Industry observers note that the following year, I was a lot more dialed in, as was the conference itself. I had regular access to a UC computer lab and understood more about the tech, skills, and culture. I was semi-regularly going to the LA 2600 meetings. More folks from the LA/Orange County scene were planning to attend. Somebody had the brilliant idea of forming a caravan. That same person had the bright idea of facilitating ride-matching between people who needed rides with people who had spare seats in their car. Unfortunately, that person also dropped out at the last minute, handing off responsibility to me and my friends, without having performed ANY of that carpool ride-matching work. This is how we ended up with “seven sweaty hackers in a Ford Escort,” with one person in the hatchback trunk space. That’s a story (and camcorder video) for another time.

According to recent reports, fast-forward two more years. By then, I was confidently (or at least, as confidently as my social anxiety and imposter syndrome would let me) running the caravan, thankfully without the ride-matching. Defcon 5 / Caravan 3 was a well-oiled machine. We had a radio antenna lashed down to the bed of a pickup truck, fed by a pirate radio station, hooked up to a mixer, microphone, and small PC providing the music files. We had timetables and routes. We even had a printed program to distribute to the participating cars!

Industry observers note that in digging through old papers, my mum ran across the zine/program for that year’s caravan. I no longer have the digital files, but I’ve scanned all of the pages as a PDF for download or as an image gallery, below.

Edit: I’m not clear on why the cover says 3 and the intro text says 4. According to my records, it was my fourth year attending, but still only the third year for the caravan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The release of Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be revolutionary in nearly every sense of the word. The latest action-adventure title from Rockstar Games has excelled so much that GTA 6 has become the best-reviewed game of all time, finally surpassing 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. A lot of this comes from how well-designed all of the features it presents are. The several gameplay mechanics, the story, the attention to detail, the technical quality, and more make for a complete package that will provide players with over 100 hours of delightful gameplay.

In Screen Rant’s review of GTA 6, we mention that it “delivers on pretty much everything it promises,” while also taking a lesson from Rockstar’s own Red Dead Redemption 2, released in 2018. The fresh release has tons of different features to use and even uncover, such as a top-down zombie survival mini-game. Even though some of the new features are the ones taking the spotlight for themselves, there are also a few classic features that make a comeback. Among the several returning mechanics, there is one that is seriously overlooked in Rockstar’s new game.

Amidst all the chaos of Vice City and the larger state of Leonida, you can potentially find some serenity by pausing the action with the game’s photo mode. Since the last entry in the series, photo modes have evolved drastically and have become foundational to most AAA games nowadays. The photo mode in Final Fantasy 16, for example, allows for some pretty spectacular images, be they of moments of tranquility or intense combat. In GTA 6, it’s not all that different, apart from the fact that it’s an entirely different setting.

According to recent reports, the upcoming photo mode allows you to take some stunning pictures in GTA 6, be they centered around characters, locations, moments, and more. As you’d expect from a feature like this, you can change the camera angle, move it around, and adjust tons of other settings, such as lighting, poses, expressions, and much more, all to create the perfect opportunity for a click. This, combined with the cutting-edge ultra-realistic graphics the game has to offer, can make for some seriously breathtaking pictures. It’s all about experimenting and playing around with the photo mode.

Not every game with a photo mode provides the right tools or the right art direction to make moments worthy of being captured, but with a game like GTA 6, photo mode is nearly a game of its own. Depending on what you’re trying to capture, you’ll spend hours moving around Leonida and changing outfits in GTA 6 to get the perfect picture.

Industry observers note that there’s no denying that Rockstar’s latest release is absolutely gorgeous. While the photo mode isn’t put in the spotlight as much as other fun features and additions to the franchise, such as the possibility of not being able to steal a vehicle or being mugged when using an ATM, the classic and ever-reliable photo mode is there, ready for you to use when you feel like capturing all the beauty Grand Theft Auto 6 has to offer.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

According to recent reports, on Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) revealed Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'.

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!".

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'.

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA confirmed the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement remarked: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) confirmed Keith Cooper had died aged 78.

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England.

Sources indicate that former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match.

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'.

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

The FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

#74436. Industry News: Vibecoding an inference chip

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2270 w)
