  • Recent findings suggest that after four flagship movies and one prequel, the franchise heads back to the past again in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” The prequel revisits Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as a teenager competing in the 50th Hunger Games.
  • In a recent development, by the time “The Hunger Games” reached its conclusion, the franchise had run out of gas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we’ve come a long way since Katniss Everdeen volunteered as tribute in “The Hunger Games.” It’s been almost 15 years since Jennifer Lawrence delivered that line and became an iconic action heroine. “The Hunger Games” brought the young adult genre to upcoming heights and proved that these movies could be legitimate blockbusters by every measure.

Recent findings suggest that after four flagship movies and one prequel, the franchise heads back to the past again in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” The prequel revisits Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as a teenager competing in the 50th Hunger Games. Where does Haymitch’s outing rank among the franchise’s best movies? Let’s get into the rankings.

In a recent development, by the time “The Hunger Games” reached its conclusion, the franchise had run out of gas. After saving a brainwashed Peeta (Josh Hutcherson), President Coin (Julianne Moore) tasks Katniss and her band of rebels with liberating District 2 before retaking the Capitol. It's the final push to overthrow President Snow, but as Katniss pursues revenge, she begins to question the rebellion’s true intentions.

Sources indicate that “The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2” isn’t necessarily a bad movie. The familiar group-on-one-last-mission trope builds to an exciting conclusion. However, it’s more concerned with reaching the finish line than saying anything fresh.

Splitting “Mockingjay” into two parts made financial sense, as the two movies combined to gross over $1.4 billion worldwide. Story-wise, a 390-page novel doesn’t need more than four hours of screen time. Whenever you end a movie on an unresolved cliffhanger, more often than not, fans are going to reject it. Guess what? Many fans, myself included, rejected the ending of “Mockingjay – Part 1.”.

According to recent reports, after being rescued from the arena in “Catching Fire,” Katniss is taken to the secret underground city of District 13. There, President Coin convinces Katniss to live up to her mockingjay reputation and become the face of the rebellion. Katniss eventually agrees to Coin’s request because she wants to save Peeta, who is being held captive in the Capitol. It’s the first movie in the franchise without the chaos of the arena, so expect less action. However, “Mockingjay – Part 1” is the best political thriller of the bunch, as it emphasizes its anti-war and anti-fascist themes the best.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that coming after the success of the four “Hunger Games” movies, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes” had low odds of achieving success, though not as low as some of the tributes entering the arena. A new cast meant the absence of Lawrence, Hutcherson, Hemsworth, and the rest of the original ensemble. Second, it’s a prequel set before the days of Katniss Everdeen. Most importantly, it’s a story about a young President Snow — yes, the same tyrannical dictator who would rule Panem for decades. How are audiences supposed to sympathize with and grow attached to the future villain of the main trilogy?

That’s the best trick “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” pulls off: no sympathy for Snow. You don’t feel sorry for him. Instead, it explores how trauma and grief can send a man down a path where embracing evil seems preferable to enduring hardship.

According to recent reports, in the film, a young Coriolanus "Coryo" Snow (Tom Blyth) mentors District 12’s Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler) in the 10th Hunger Games. It’s the most grounded arena battle in the franchise, and the violence feels worse than ever before. It’s a fascinating origin story that had no business being this effective.

Recent findings suggest that “The Hunger Games” is known for having a deep bench of talented supporting actors. Woody Harrelson famously played Haymitch Abernathy, a former winner of the Games who mentored Katniss and Peeta in District 12. Haymitch was first introduced as a drunk and despondent former victor who wanted nothing to do with the Hunger Games. As the movies progressed, viewers learned that Haymitch was one of the rebellion’s allies and had been for a long time.

According to recent reports, why was Haymitch depressed all those years? “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” fills in the blanks, as it revisits Haymitch’s win in the 50th Hunger Games, the second Quarter Quell. Zada stars as the 16-year-old Haymitch, who is much happier thanks to the love of his family and girlfriend, Lenora Dove Baird (Whitney Peak).

After witnessing the Capitol’s hostility, Haymitch becomes the key figure in a plot to sabotage the Games once and for all. It’s a tad too long, but this movie soars because of Zada, who injects so much life and passion into his portrayal of Haymitch. It’s a true movie-star-in-the-making performance. Don’t be surprised if Marvel or DC is calling Zada to put on a cape in a few years.

The movie that kicked off the young adult dystopian movie wave was 2012’s “The Hunger Games.” On the day of the reaping, Katniss volunteers to take her younger sister’s place in the 74th Hunger Games. Katniss and Peeta, her fellow District 12 tribute, enter the arena with little hope of surviving. As the Games progress, Katniss reluctantly becomes a symbol of hope, and her defiance lays the foundation for a rebellion.

“The Hunger Games” was revolutionary for its time. It proved a young adult action franchise could be a profitable endeavor ($695 million worldwide). Lawrence became a legitimate star and rose to A-list status, which she maintains in 2026. The movie depicts a battle to the death, but its messages about authoritarianism, exploitation, and inequality are very sophisticated for a teen drama. Plus, it breaks an unwritten Hollywood rule—don’t kill kids. I commend the film for having the guts to show Rue’s death. Throw your 3s in the air!

According to recent reports, there was only one answer. I consider myself a “real fan” of “The Hunger Games,” and real ones know that “Catching Fire” is the best book and movie in the franchise. It’s the best action movie of the bunch, with the most innovative arena, a top-notch supporting cast, and riveting twists. After Katniss and Peeta defy the Capitol, President Snow makes the duo parade around the districts to eliminate civil unrest.

When that doesn’t work, Snow announces a twist for the 75th Hunger Games: All tributes will be former winners. In other words, it’s back to the arena for Katniss and Peeta. “Catching Fire” has by far the best in-arena sequences, with my favorite scene being the opening of the Games, where Katniss teams up with her upcoming ally (Finnick) to save Peeta. Forget the young adult genre; “Catching Fire” is an excellent action movie that improves upon its predecessor in nearly every way.

Here are the 3 PS5 settings you need to check to enhance your GTA 6 experience.

Sources indicate that this one is for folks who own an OLED TV. In the Video Output tab in System Settings, scroll down to HDR. Click it, and you’ll be taken to another screen to calibrate the console’s HDR.

It has been revealed that you’ll adjust the brightness across three pages. On the first two pages, press up or down until the sun logo disappears. On the last page, dial it all the way down, since your OLED TV can display deep blacks.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 also has in-game HDR calibration. Just follow the on-screen prompts to get your desired result, though I’ve found the default settings work well.

Industry observers note that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 is undoubtedly a feast for the eyes, but you shouldn’t neglect the audio side of the equation.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, while the PS5 didn’t launch with Dolby Atmos, it now supports the feature. So if you have a soundbar or surround sound system that supports Dolby Atmos, you should definitely enable it. To do so, go to Sound in System Settings, click Sound Output, scroll down to Audio Format, and select Dolby Atmos.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on all consoles. Rockstar Games even confirmed to Kotaku that the PS5 Pro won’t be patched to run at 40 or 60 fps. That said, we can’t completely rule it out.

If GTA 6 ever adds a performance-enhancing feature, you’ll want to set the PS5 Pro for that. In the Video Output tab of the Screen and Audio settings, make sure that VRR is set to Automatic for unsupported games and that 120Hz output is set to Automatic.

Recent findings suggest that again, this won’t make GTA 6 run at a higher frame rate, but it prepares your PS5 Pro if it ever does. As a rule of thumb, you should have these settings enabled anyway, since many PlayStation titles offer 40 fps modes.

Until we get the inevitable PC version of GTA 6, we'll have to make do with the experience on existing consoles, in this case, the PS5. That mentioned, the advice I've given you should help you get the most from the game. Have fun in Vice City!

#74378. Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1502 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Valkey ↗ Open Full Page

Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Valkey

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A sorted set can spend more memory describing how its elements are ordered than storing the elements themselves.
  • In Valkey 9.2 that changes: the skiplist is replaced by a high-fanout B+ tree variant called fbtree.
  • According to recent reports, fbtree combines the high fanout and contiguous storage of a conventional B+ tree with several optimizations designed for Valkey's workload and memory allocator, including feature-based lookups, SIMD searches, linked leaves, and fast paths for sequential inserts and pops.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A sorted set can spend more memory describing how its elements are ordered than storing the elements themselves.

In Valkey 9.2 that changes: the skiplist is replaced by a high-fanout B+ tree variant called fbtree.

According to recent reports, fbtree combines the high fanout and contiguous storage of a conventional B+ tree with several optimizations designed for Valkey's workload and memory allocator, including feature-based lookups, SIMD searches, linked leaves, and fast paths for sequential inserts and pops. In a 5-million-member test, it reduced per-member memory overhead by 36–43%, saving up to 109 MB.

Let's take a look at why this change happened and how it works.

In a recent development, large sorted sets that exceed the listpack threshold are backed by a skiplist paired with a hashtable (smaller sorted sets use a compact listpack representation that stores elements sequentially in contiguous memory). The hashtable gives O(1) lookups by member, while the skiplist gives O(log n) ordered lookups by rank or score. That pairing is architecturally simple, but the skiplist carries a significant memory cost. It stores exactly one element per node, scattered across memory as separate allocations connected by pointers.

Valkey's skiplist pays for this in raw memory. Every node carries a backward pointer (8B), plus an average of 1.33 levels of forward pointers and span values, since skiplists are probabilistic (each node has a 25% chance of gaining another level). Each level costs 8B for the pointer plus 8B for the span value, giving around 29B of pointer and span overhead per node. Add the 8B score, and the total reaches roughly 37B per node before accounting for the member string.

Modern CPUs use a hierarchy of hardware caches (L1, L2, and L3) to keep frequently accessed data close to the processor. These caches are much smaller and faster than main memory (RAM), so when the CPU cannot find the data it needs in its cache, it must fetch it from a slower level of the memory hierarchy. As a rough illustration, an L1 cache hit can take about 1 ns, while a DRAM access can take around 100 ns. A dependent memory access can leave the core waiting; actual latency and how much work can be hidden vary by system and workload 1.

Each node in the skiplist is a separate allocation, potentially scattered wherever the heap happened to place it, so following the structure can require repeatedly fetching data from unrelated memory locations. Because each step can determine where the next step goes, these fetches are dependent, resulting in more round trips through the memory hierarchy. A 2025 study of concurrent in-memory indexes found that, on its tested workloads, traditional skiplists experienced roughly 2.4–4.8× more cache misses than a comparable B-tree, with 2–8× lower throughput 2 (testing different data structure implementations, not Valkey).

Recent findings suggest that A B+ tree keeps entries sorted in fixed-size nodes: leaf nodes hold the entries, or pointers to them, and inner nodes hold just enough routing data to pick which child to descend into. Packing many entries into each node addresses both problems above: far less per-member pointer overhead, and far fewer dependent fetches per lookup.

fbtree, short for Feature B+ Tree, uses a 61-way fanout: each node can hold up to 61 entries or child pointers. Leaf and inner nodes are sized to fit jemalloc allocation classes without wasting space on 64-bit builds; on supported 32-bit builds, innerNode is rounded up to the 1280-byte class.

A 512-byte leaf holds up to 61 value pointers, so 61 members share one node instead of each getting its own. Instead of storing the score and member separately, fbtree stores them together as a single packed value: the normalized 8-byte score followed by the member bytes. This keeps the data needed for comparisons together and removes another level of pointer indirection.

The skiplist's 25%-per-level rule gives it an effective branching factor of about 4, while fbtree's fanout is 61. Both structures retain O(log n) search complexity, but the B+ tree has substantially fewer levels to traverse and therefore fewer opportunities for expensive memory fetches.

A modern CPU can also fetch several adjacent cache lines efficiently when the data is laid out contiguously, thanks in part to the way memory is accessed and to hardware prefetching 1. Therefore a B+ tree node that spans a few cache lines can be read efficiently as the CPU scans its contents.

On top of that structure, fbtree adds optimizations aimed at specific operations.

In a recent development, in a B+ tree keyed by variable-length strings, such as sorted set members, picking a child means comparing the lookup against each child’s anchor, the largest member in that child, and reading those strings costs memory fetches. fbtree's inner nodes store each anchor along with a small four-byte "feature." Because the anchors often share a common prefix, fbtree stores that shared prefix separately and uses the four feature bytes to distinguish the children. The implementation can then compare those features in parallel using SIMD, often identifying the correct child before fetching the child node itself. If the features uniquely identify a child, the search can descend immediately; otherwise, they still narrow the range that needs a full binary search.

According to recent reports, range commands such as ZRANGE walk the set in order. fbtree links its leaf nodes in a doubly-linked list, so a scan can move from leaf to leaf without climbing back up the tree. The skiplist requests an item, waits to receive it, and only knows the next item to fetch when it's received the first. The B+ tree can work on up to 61 items in parallel, and while it works on those it can fetch the next leaf node with the next 61 items.

Commands such as ZPOPMIN work at the ends of the set. fbtree caches its leftmost and rightmost leaves, so finding them is O(1), as in a skiplist, instead of O(log n). This keeps pop and append operations at parity rather than regressing.

Range deletions remove a contiguous run of members, and fbtree handles them without rebuilding the surrounding structure.

According to recent reports, the change is internal: sorted set commands and their behavior remain unchanged. The one visible difference is that OBJECT ENCODING returns btree instead of skiplist for a large sorted set. If you have monitoring, tests, or tooling that checks for the literal string skiplist, that's one place to update. Small sorted sets under the listpack threshold are unaffected either way, since they never used the skiplist encoding to begin with.

The numbers below compare only the ordered index: skiplist versus fbtree, with the hashtable and member embedding unchanged.

Inserting 5 million 20-byte members sequentially reduced per-member memory overhead, excluding the member data itself, from 50.3B to 28.5B, a 43% reduction. The same 5 million members inserted in random order reduced per-member overhead from 50.3B to 32.0B, a 36% reduction.

The smaller reduction comes from random insertion leaving more partially filled nodes than sequential insertion.

Sources indicate that for the 5-million-member set in this test, that is roughly 109 MB saved with sequential inserts and 92 MB with random inserts. The savings are per member, not per byte stored, so the relative reduction in total memory is largest for sets with many small members and shrinks as member size grows.

The benchmarks below were measured on PR #4206’s oi/pr3-fbtree-v2 branch and were not rerun for the merged commit. They were run on a Graviton3 c7g.metal system with 64 cores, nine I/O threads, a pipeline depth of 10, and a 3-million-member sorted set. Each test was repeated five times; the reported confidence intervals were ≤2% for all commands except ZRANDMEMBER.

The same underlying design changes also improve throughput for several sorted set operations:.

Industry observers note that ZADD and ZREM reposition elements in the tree, so they gain the most from fbtree's shallower structure and fewer pointer updates. Range operations see smaller gains because once the index traversal becomes cheap, producing and returning the requested elements becomes a larger part of the total cost. ZSCORE and ZRANDMEMBER barely move because they use the hashtable, not the ordered index.

The notable takeaway: the commands didn't change, but in our tests large sorted sets carried 36–43% less per-member overhead, and ZADD and ZREM throughput rose 105% and 76%.

The goal wasn't simply to make the data structure faster in isolation: the implementation was repeatedly benchmarked against the existing skiplist through the full Valkey server, with optimizations added until fbtree matched or exceeded the skiplist across the tested sorted set commands.

Valkey 9.2 is presently in release-candidate testing. Before GA, try the 9.2 release candidate with your real workload, especially if large sorted sets or commands such as ZADD, ZREM, ZRANK, or ZCOUNT are important to you. Your testing and feedback can help surface problems before the final release, so open an issue with anything you find.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026.

Hamilton Academical 1 Ross County 2.

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving Upcoming Douglas Park.

Sources indicate that the decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

County, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Industry observers note that scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so New Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County.

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he mentioned. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’.

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he said. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’.

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he noted: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’.

According to recent reports, edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he mentioned.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek.

Recent findings suggest that with 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ mentioned Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’.

The Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ said McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

It has been revealed that ‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ remarked McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’.

Recent findings suggest that there was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’.

He added: ‘The new guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’.

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

‘It’s about loyalty,’ he noted. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’.

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he said. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’.

A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he mentioned. ‘This season we are going up.’.

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game.

Brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

He was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he remarked. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’.

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he said.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County.

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he remarked. ‘We are scoring team goals.’.

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’.

Sources indicate that it was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he remarked.

He added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’.

Sources indicate that asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he noted: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’.

According to recent reports, there is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

Latest Update: Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (939 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in a latest filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • Apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in a latest filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a newly introduced filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its newly introduced filing, Epic indicates Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the company of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

In a recent development, apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple states decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s upcoming CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Sources indicate that under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

According to recent reports, given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a newly introduced order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

Industry observers note that one of those standout live TV streaming services is Fubo. The popular service offers hundreds of channels in a selection of well-priced packages. If you’re looking to ditch cable — or find a way to access channels you lost by cutting the cord — it’s a great option.

Sports + News: Fubo’s Sports + News plan is a streamlined, affordable option that costs $64.99 a month. You get 30+ channels, including local stations (ABC, CBS, NBC, and FOX), Fox News, and sports channels like ESPN, FS1, and NFL Network.

Elite: Fubo’s largest package is Elite, which offers over 250 channels and — unlike the options above — 4K UHD high-resolution streaming for certain content. It costs $98.99 a month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a upcoming Morgan Stanley research report states Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which debuted only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

According to recent reports, apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

It has been revealed that back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That remarked, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

When it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone owners surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was revealed, but before it launched, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less key in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the problem.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks. The BBC contacted the FBI for comment.

Industry observers note that this comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyberattacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with US President Donald Trump saying he was not good enough.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US.

In September, the FBI noted it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) .

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC mentioned.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the glitch.

  • At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid aims for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid aims for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp users running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

Users can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot presently be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning owners switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for customers running the public version without requiring another app update.

The Best Music Moments and Surprise Cameos From ‘GTA VI’

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here.
  • Once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts.
  • The game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here. Music, of course, is integral to all of it. There’s a soundtrack full of stars — the 34-track release, which is out today, features Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Arca, and more. In addition to that, there is a massive one-day festival inspired by the game, taking place in Miami on Nov. 21, with headliners Cardi B, Metro Boomin, and Justice, who also put together the game’s score.

Once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts. Here are some of the best music moments and surprise cameos from the biggest video game of the year.

The game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back. There’s Cocoteo FM hosted by Bad Bunny and RaiNao, Back Country Radio hosted by Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey, and Radio La Ola with Gloria and Emilio Estefan, plus tons more. But one that may surprise people is Stockyard FM, featuring two DJs named Victoria and Harrison — better known as PinkPantheress and the Dare. Victoria and Harrison are their real names, and their radio station is dedicated to experimental, left-of-center pop, electronica, and indie sleaze.

One of the GTA VI radio stations, Radio La Ola, plays homage to Latin classics from over the decades. But one hugely surprising one is “Sopa de Caracol,” a massive but somewhat forgotten hit from the Nineties by Honduran band Banda Blanca. The inclusion made headlines in Central America, with the lead singer Pilo Tejada saying he was honored to have his voice reach new parts of the world.

Sources indicate that psych-rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard is featured on the soundtrack: They’re one of several artists on the collaboration “Flower in a Hurricane,” which also earned them their first Billboard 100 entry. But that’s not the only place you can find them: Gizz fans noticed that throughout several parts of the game, you can hear snippets of what appear to be demos from the band, woven into the score. On Reddit, diehards have been pointing these out and playing guessing games as they wonder what projects these might be from.

We’ve known that the French electronic duo Justice composed the original score for the game, but the official album won’t be out until Dec. 11. We’re getting to hear some of what they came up with the release of the game but there’s still more to come, including an anticipated collaboration with the Weeknd. The duo have since mentioned this is the “first and last” video game they’ll ever score.

Industry observers note that the soundtrack, which dropped on Nov. 19, is packed, featuring 34 songs by some surprising artists and stars. There’s new music from Travis Scott, the Fuerza Regida track “Suzuki,” which is charting in 15 countries, and there are also songs from Keith Richards, Kali Uchis and Helado Negro, and more. A lot of the music was inspired directly by Miami, which you can hear in new tracks from artists like JT.

Artists are getting into the game, too. Tinashe delighted fans with a hilarious livestream playing for the first time. The stream captured her making an epic getaway by flying an airplane and hysterically crashing it into the ground, then running out of ammo in a shootout. “I have no bullets!” she screams. “Holy shit, I’m going to have to beat the fuck out of them myself.” After several days of sold-out highlights in the U.K., Noah Kahan stayed up late and wreaked havoc in Vice City while his wife was asleep.

The world lost D’Angelo back in 2025, but his legacy lives on in Vice City. GTA VI players discovered that an unreleased track called “Kamakazi,” as confirmed by D’Angelo collaborator DJ Dojah, is one of the songs you can hear on the radio station Worldwide FM. D’Angelo’s “Lady” also plays on the in-game Honey FM channel, which is hosted by Chilli and T-Boz of TLC.

While the creators of the game spent a ton of time adding interesting radio stations and track to the GTA VI universe, there is plenty of love for pop stars and major pop hits. Dua Lipa appears on the soundtrack, but the radio stations also feature plenty of pop girlies: There’s Chappell Roan’s “Hot To Go!,” Charli XCX’s “Good Ones,” and Addison Rae’s “Fame Is a Gun,” just to name a few, which players can blast while driving through Vice City.

The Oura Ring 5 holds the title of the "world's smallest smart ring", with a focus on a slim design and lightweight barely-there feel.

Sources indicate that after wearing the Oura Ring 5 for five months, I must say that it lives up to its title. Not once have I ever felt any discomfort from wearing the ring, with its sleep design never interfering with my sleep. Thanks to the sizing kit, it fits like a glove, too.

Sources indicate that the Oura Ring 5's fit was a breath of fresh air compared to the Apple Watch Ultra that I wore to bed for a few months before I obtained the Oura Ring 5. Granted, the Apple Watch Ultra is a lot bigger and bulkier than the newer Apple Watch models, such as the Apple Watch 12.

Sources indicate that but all Apple Watches are exactly that: watches. I find any wristwatch uncomfortable to wear in bed, particularly smartwatches with heavy screens and tight straps (you need plenty of skin contact for tracking accuracy). But that's a personal preference and if you don't mind something bulky on your wrist in bed, you might sleep happily in the Apple Watch 12.

As for the Garmin, the lead tester in our Garmin Index Sleep Monitor review found the armband design to be surprisingly comfortable and lightweight. The band is available in two sizes (S-M and L-XL), and its screen-free design means it isn't weighed down by heavy monitors.

Industry observers note that when it comes down to it, the Oura, Apple, and Garmin sleep trackers share a lot of core sleep tracking features. For example, not only do all three tell you how long you slept, but also how much of that sleep duration was spent in deep sleep, REM sleep, and core sleep (along with how long your night-time awakenings last). They also all provide sleep scores, which measure your overall sleep quality on a scale of 1 to 100.

Sources indicate that you can find the key sleep metrics in the Oura app, Garmin Connect app, and the Apple Health app respectively. For the screenless Oura and Garmin, this is the only way to view your sleep data. But you get immediate feedback from your Apple Watch via the Vitals app on the monitor.

The Oura Ring 5 is designed to provide more sleep tracking accuracy than the Oura Ring 4, with a build that improves the sensors' contact with skin and 12% more accuracy in its overnight Heart Rate Variability (HRV) monitoring.

I've found the Oura Ring one of the most dependable consumer sleep trackers on the market. It's especially good at knowing when you're asleep vs awake; studies show up to 96% accuracy when compared to clinical polysomnography (PSG).

I can see the Oura Ring 5's accuracy first hand. When I wore the Oura Ring 5 and the Apple Watch (Ultra) at the same time, I felt the Oura Ring's data reflected how I felt in the morning more accurately than the Apple Watch. For instance, my Apple Watch sleep scores are always much higher than my Oura Ring — despite regularly getting under seven hours of sleep.

That said, the Apple Watch does provide a sleep apnea detection tool (available on the Apple Watch Series 10 and up), which analyzes your breathing patterns to detect disturbances that might signal sleep apnea.

Meanwhile, the Garmin Index Sleep Monitor provides a readiness score, which tells you how prepared your body is to handle daily activities (such as workouts) based on your sleep data.

It has been revealed that our lead tester for the Garmin Index Sleep Monitor, Eve Davies, said that the Garmin is "more focused on overnight breathing rates, oxygen levels and respiration rates — is essentially more ‘nerdy’ and geared towards athletic recovery". For data lovers, there's a lot to unpack.

It's also worth mentioning that the Oura Ring 5's sleep latency metric is missing from the Apple Watch and Index Sleep Monitor. And its unique circadian scoring, which uses sleep data over time to identify your sleep chronotype, can help you identify how well your sleep routine aligns with your circadian rhythm.

Sources indicate that the Oura Ring 5 is designed to provide around six to nine days of battery life on a single charge. A full charge (from zero to 100) is said to take up to 80 minutes, though I find it charges much faster than this.

That said, I've never found that my ring's battery life has lasted nine days (or even a full week), but this may be due to the fact that I wear a size 7 — the smaller sizes have a shorter battery life.

However, the lifespan of an Oura Ring is that of a giant tortoise when compared with the Apple Watch. The Apple Watch requires daily charging, with the latest 12th Generation's battery life lasting no longer than 24 hours.

The Garmin has quite a lengthy battery life, lasting up to eight nights (however, this can depend on your sleep duration). However, you also wear it less than the Oura Ring 5 or Apple Watch — if you strapped it to yourself all day, expect that battery life to go right down.

✅ You want in-depth sleep tracking: The Oura Ring 5's accuracy is renowned, while its unique sleep features (such as its Body Clock feature) sets it apart.

✅ You value optimal sleep comfort: Thanks to a custom fit and a sleek, lightweight build, the Oura Ring 5 is perfect for a barely-there feel.

✅ You don't own an iPhone: You need an iPhone to set up your Apple Watch, so consider the Oura Ring 5 if you're an Android user.

✅ You don't want to pay monthly fees: The Apple Watch has no hidden subscription costs.

✅ You want immediate feedback: With a screen to view your metrics, the Apple Watch is the only option that doesn't require fiddling about with an app.

✅ You want more versatility: There's a lot more to the Apple Watch than sleep tracking, including highly-rated fitness tracking, and there are plenty of models to suit your requirements.

✅ You want the most budget-friendly tracker: The Garmin Index Sleep Monitor is never sold over $170, and you can reliably find it on sale during holiday seasons.

✅ You just want a sleep tracker: While the Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch put a lot of energy into fitness and health tracking, the Garmin Index Sleep Monitor is strictly for sleep tracking.

✅ You want a long battery life: The Garmin Index Sleep Monitor can last up to eight nights on a single charge.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another firm is having an outage.
  • Recent findings suggest that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another firm is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication issues." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

Recent findings suggest that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering latest security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Industry observers note that mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find new security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be stated for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

According to recent reports, you might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October enhancement. The organization's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's important to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

Barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as rapidly as possible.

Sources indicate that the implications aren't specific to any one company, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Industry observers note that of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that iFixit’s teardown of the latest Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Recent findings suggest that percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

Percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • UPDATED, 5:50 PM: A Los Angeles jury has convicted the man charged with setting the smoldering fire that later flared up into Palisades Fire that devastated Pacific Palisades and Malibu in early 2025.
  • Industry observers note that rinderknecht faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in state prison when he is sentenced on March 17.
  • Back in June, a separate jury deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquitting Rinderknecht on similar charges including a third for timber set afire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED, 5:50 PM: A Los Angeles jury has convicted the man charged with setting the smoldering fire that later flared up into Palisades Fire that devastated Pacific Palisades and Malibu in early 2025. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was found guilty Friday of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

Industry observers note that rinderknecht faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in state prison when he is sentenced on March 17. He has been in federal custody since October 2025. See the bottom of this post for the the Justice Department’s detailed account of Rinderknecht’s movements on the night the first fire started and its case against him.

Back in June, a separate jury deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquitting Rinderknecht on similar charges including a third for timber set afire. Prosecutors dropped that last charge, and the In the new indictment, the first charge referred only to Rinderknecht’s setting of the Lachman Fire on New Year’s Eve, rather than the Lachman and Palisades fires. The Lachman Fire smoldered for a week before Santa Ana winds re-ignited the flames. Watch on Deadline.

During the just-ended trial, Assistant U.S. Attorney Matt O’Brien argued that Rinderknecht was consumed by anger, loneliness and a thirst for revenge, prompting him to use a grill lighter to ignite hilltop vegetation around midnight on Dec. 31, 2024, at the remote, deserted area adjacent to the Pacific Palisades’ Summit neighborhood. But defense lawyer Steven Haney argued there was no direct evidence proving that his client set the earlier fire, saying the prosecution’s case lacked any witnesses to the alleged crime and consisted only of circumstantial allegations.

The Los Angeles Fire Department issued in a statement Friday after the verdict. “We respect the jury’s work and the long, difficult process that brought us to today’s verdict,” it reads in part. “Our first thought is with the families of those we lost and for everyone in our community whose lives were changed by this fire. No verdict, however key, could ever undo that loss.”.

It has been revealed that the Palisades Fire was the most destructive blaze in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people, burning 23,448 acres, costing billions in damage and insurance claims, and ruining much of the exclusive Pacific Palisades community, destroying about 6,500 structures across the Palisades and Malibu. Read more details below, and see the full news release from the U.S. Department of Justice at the bottom of this post.

PREVIOUSLY, June 25: The jury charged with determining if Jonathan Rinderknecht is guilty of starting the blaze in early 2025 that became the devastating Palisades Fire can’t come up with a verdict, yet.

“The jury in the Jonathan Rinderknecht trial sent a subsequent note saying they are deadlocked,” the Justice Department tells Deadline today. “The trial continues.”.

How long the trial continues now or if a mistrial is declared becomes the vital questions. U.S. District Court Judge Anne Hwang has instructed the jury to return on Friday morning to take another kick at the can.

A note from the jurors read out in court earlier this afternoon in downtown L.A. by the judge set the stage. “We have people on both sides that are dead set, unwavering and unwilling to change their opinion,” the note, the second of the day, said. It went on to say: “We are at a standstill and unsure of how to proceed.”.

In a recent development, ex-Uber driver Rinderknecht has always insisted he is innocent of the charges and being put up as a fall guy for the failures of civic leaders and First Responders. If a mistrial is declared in this instance, the feds could attempt another trial with a fresh jury and hope for a better outcome.

According to recent reports, after just over a day of deliberations on the arson charges after a 10-day trial, the jurors indicated they had a verdict just over 90 minutes ago. The currently incarcerated Rinderknecht, his defense team, prosecutors and various local, state and federal officials were brought into court after the judge was informed there was a “unanimous verdict.”.

What they finally did hear left Judge Hwang in clear angst.

While there was some confusion initially over when their decision would be read out in court, and the clocked ticked away, it is now clear the case is in serious trouble — even as it continues.

Sources indicate that looking at up to 45 years behind bars if found guilty, Rinderknecht was, in Department of Justice documents filed last fall, “indicted on one count of Destruction of Property by Means of Fire (18 U.S.C. § 844(f)(1)); one count of Arson Affecting Property Used in Interstate Commerce (18 U.S.C. § 844(i)); and one count of Timber Set Afire (18 U.S.C. § 1855), in a case arising out of the Lachman/Palisades Fire in January 2025.”.

Today’s verdict or lack there of, will continue the frustration many feel over the wildfires, the response and the consequences. While some reconstruction has taken place in the Palisades, as well as Malibu and out of the Eaton Fire that tore through Altadena, progress has been slow and stymied by all metrics.

Industry observers note that A major factor in the ongoing L.A. mayoral race, and the spark for the unsuccessful insurgency campaign of ex-Palisades resident and Hills alum Spencer Pratt, the fires and the fallout hang heavy over the city and the community as another sign of a metropolis that has lost its way — even more so this past week with the just extinguished cold storage warehouse fire in Boyle Heights that prompted air quality and other health warnings.

Sources indicate that the subject of an intense investigation by various branches of government both national and state, Rinderknecht was arrested in Florida on October 8 last year. The then 29-year-old is accused of intentionally starting a “hold over” fire the week before that eventually sparked into the Palisades Fire.

Placed at the scene by his own iPhone and failed 9-1-1 calls, Rinderknecht later that New Year’s Day morning drove away from the area as LAFD started arriving on the scene, making a gesture to assist the firefighters, the DOJ’s filing of last year asserted.

It has been revealed that A week later the same fire, which even after LAFD has been on the scene, had likely smoldered underground, reemerged and became known as the Palisades Fire. Destroying most of the Hollywood heavy community, the Palisades Fire killed more than a dozen people and decimated over 5,400 homes.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this week, after closing arguments, defense lawyer Steve Haney entered a motion to have the case dismissed based on lack of compelling evidence by the feds. With the bevy of online postings and asking AI platforms if you could start a fire with a lit cigarette, as well as Rinderknecht’s involvement with the January 1, 2025 Lachman Fire that preceded the Palisades Fire, that dismissal effort was dismissed pretty rapidly by Judge Hwang.

More such motions from the defense may be in the offering ASAP if this deadlocked situation continues into next week.

Here is the Justice Department’s post-verdict news release:.

According to recent reports, A former Los Angeles resident was found guilty by a jury today of starting what became the Palisades Fire of January 2025, the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, a.k.a. “Jonathan Rinder,” and “Jon Rinder,” was found guilty of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” mentioned Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”According to evidence presented at a 14-day trial, on January 1, 2025, Rinderknecht ignited what came to be known as the Lachman and Palisades fires.In the days leading up to the Lachman Fire, Rinderknecht exhibited extreme anger, indignation, and frustration about being unable to find companionship on New Year’s Eve 2024 and about a former co-worker whom he briefly dated in March 2024.Alone on New Year’s Eve, Rinderknecht drove several Uber passengers, nearly all of whom remembered him being angry that night. He dropped off his final Uber passenger in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles and drove to The Summit, a neighborhood where he had lived a few years earlier with a former lover.Rinderknecht drove towards Skull Rock Trailhead, parked his car, attempted to contact a former friend, and walked up the trail. He then used his iPhone to take videos at a nearby hilltop area and listened to a rap song – to which he had listened repeatedly in previous days – whose music video included things being lit on fire.When Rinderknecht maliciously started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, he was alone in a small clearing on Hidden Buddha Hill in Pacific Palisades.At approximately 12:12 a.m. on January 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman Fire had begun. During the next five minutes, Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of cellphone range. When he finally connected with 911, he was at the bottom of the hiking trail and reported the fire. By that point, a nearby resident already had reported the fire to authorities.Rinderknecht then fled in his car, passing fire engines driving in the opposite direction. He then turned around and followed the fire engines to the scene, driving at a high rate of speed. Rinderknecht walked up the same trail from earlier that night to watch the fire and the firefighters. At approximately 1:02 a.m., he used his iPhone to take more videos of the scene.During an interview with law enforcement on January 24, 2025, Rinderknecht lied about where he was when he first saw the Lachman Fire. He claimed he was near the bottom of a hiking trail when he first saw the fire and called 911, but geolocation data from his iPhone carrier revealed that he was standing in a clearing 30 feet from the fire as it rapidly grew.Although firefighters promptly suppressed the Lachman Fire, the fire continued to smolder and burn underground within the root structure of dense vegetation.On January 7, 2025, heavy winds caused the underground fire to surface and spread above ground in what became known as the Palisades Fire, which caused widespread damage in Pacific Palisades, killing 12 people, and destroyed 6,837 structures, causing an estimated $25 billion in damage in the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.United States District Judge Anne Hwang scheduled a March 17, 2027 sentencing hearing, at which time Rinderknecht would face a mandatory minimum sentence of five years in federal prison and a statutory maximum sentence of 40 years in federal prison.Rinderknecht has been in federal custody since October 2025.The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is investigating this matter with substantial assistance from the Los Angeles Police Department and the United States Forest Service.Assistant United States Attorneys Mark A. Williams, Matthew W. O’Brien, and Danbee C. Kim of the Environmental Crimes and Consumer Protection Section are prosecuting this case.If you are a victim of the Palisades Fire, updates about this criminal case can be found on this webpage.

Erik Pedersen and City News Service contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple today announced that App Store prices for apps and In-App Purchases will be adjusted in five countries starting December 3, following changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates. Here are the details.

In a upcoming post published on its developer portal, Apple today announced a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the company, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple stated that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

It has been revealed that apple added that a new “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and enhancement their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor mentioned.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'.
