Sources indicate that the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus is an admirable entry-level soundbar. Although it won’t beat any of the major names unlike its cheaper sibling, the TV Soundbar, it provides an instant TV speaker upgrade without breaking the bank.

Built-in subwoofer with adjustable bass volume.

Bass can overpower dialogue in action scenes.

According to recent reports, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Price: 4/5Sound quality: 3/5Design: 4/5Features: 3/5Overall score: 3.5/5Best for: The space-conscious, budget-conscious, subwoofer-wanters.

All-in-one soundbars are a dangerous game. How does one balance center channels for dialogue with a subwoofer for the best blockbuster movie action? In the case of the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus, with semi-difficulty.

In a recent development, don’t get me wrong, the price is incredibly appealing — $249 for a 3.1-channel soundbar is super affordable — and the minimalist design won’t cause any controversy. But is this enough to make it one of the best soundbars?

Industry observers note that yes and no. Unfortunately, the bass tends to overpower dialogue in action-heavy scenes. But could this still be the soundbar for you if you only watch TV and YouTube? Find out in this Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus review.

If you’re looking for a reason to buy the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus, that sweet, sweet MSRP is the biggest one.

Sources indicate that at $249 at Amazon U.S. ($139 on sale) and £249 at Amazon U.K., the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus is incredibly cheap for what you get. It’s an all-in-one “Dolby Atmos” soundbar — yes, that means with a built-in subwoofer. The basic model, Amazon Fire TV Soundbar, is $119, so you’re essentially paying $130 for a built-in subwoofer.

At this price point, there’s very little competition. Of course, there’s the Samsung B750F ($297, 2025 model), which has a separate subwoofer and 5.1 channels (more upfiring speakers for better surround sound). Even so, this is $50 pricier, which can be a dealbreaker if you’re on a rigid budget.

I’ve also tested the Samsung Q600F — MSRP of $499 but often on sale in the $300s — which is 2025’s model but has a 3.1.2 channel setup, which is the minimum you need for genuine Dolby Atmos. I’ll get into this more below, but that’s the long and short of it.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Recent findings suggest that the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is $349 with a 3.1 channel — so the same as the Amazon Plus and without the surround channels present on the Samsung Q600F — which I would recommend over the Plus if you have a little more to spare. Its separate subwoofer provides a stronger bass response without overpowering dialogue, unlike the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus.

Like the $119 Amazon Fire TV Soundbar, the Plus model also has EQ modes. These are as follows: “Music”, “Movie”, “Sports”, and “Night”. There’s also individual bass level adjustment if you want to get really particular with your listening experience.

There's a dialogue mode, but this didn't isolate speech as well as I wanted it to, especially in louder, action-heavy scenes.

Sources indicate that music mode (connected via Bluetooth) is fine, although the bass was a little boomy and the vocals a little too sharp. I would recommend grabbing one of the best speakers, like the JBL Flip 7, to listen to music at home.

So let’s get one thing straight: the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus does not have “true” Dolby Atmos. If a soundbar doesn’t have side-firing or up-firing channel speakers, it physically cannot project soundwaves in that way.

In Top Gun: Maverick's dogfighting scene, I could feel the soundtrack whoosh around me, and the radioed dialogue sounded as if it were coming from beside the TV.

Recent findings suggest that however, the Plus has “Dolby Atmos”, which means it can technically decode Atmos signals. While this obviously doesn’t produce a genuinely immersive experience, it does have its moments. In the dogfighting scene in "Top Gun: Maverick," I could feel the soundtrack whoosh around me, and the radioed dialogue sounded as if it were coming from beside the TV. As I’ll get into later, this pushed the dialogue to the back of the soundstage, resulting in me straining to hear speech.

Dolby Atmos was better in “K-Pop Demon Hunters, which is really surprising. Usually, “Top Gun: Maverick” blows other movies out of the water in terms of Atmos. Cheering crowds were louder and more immersive in “K-Pop Demon Hunters," and some dialogue was positioned well in the up-firing speakers. One character's voice was particularly crisp and immersive — the lowest female voice — which makes me think the soundbar is better at isolating lower mids than sub-bass.

Industry observers note that despite having a range of EQ modes and a palatable price, unfortunately, the Plus gets a 3.5-star rating from me for a reason. There's one majorly crucial thing holding it back.

In a recent development, unlike the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar, the Plus really struggles to differentiate between dialogue and bass layers in action-heavy scenes. “Top Gun: Maverick” was particularly egregious here: Bass often overpowered dialogue, especially when the soundtrack was relatively heavy in flying scenes. I could barely hear Maverick's radioed dialogue to the characters in the control room over the string-heavy soundtrack and the flying airplane.

This was incredibly surprising, as the cheaper non-Plus model excelled in the very same scene. Bass volume was set to the minimum, and I watched on “Movie” mode.

Sources indicate that while not as egregious in “K-Pop Demon Hunters," I still struggled to hear some dialogue. Surprisingly, the music sounded excellent in this movie, but dialogue is arguably the most vital part. If you can’t hear the actors, what’s the point?

The consequences are really enormous: I struggled to make out dialogue in action-heavy scenes across the three movies I watched, which isn’t really what you want when using a soundbar. The whole purpose of a soundbar is to make dialogue more intelligible.

However, I also watched "Gilmore Girls" on basic Netflix, which sounded great. If you predominantly watch TV or YouTube, I don't think you'll notice this problem. It's just a concern for action movie buffs. In that case, I'd recommend checking out the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer ($375).

At $249, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is incredibly affordable. There are very few soundbars that can beat this in terms of penny-per-performance.

The aforementioned Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is $349, so $100 more than the Amazon model, but has a dedicated subwoofer and a center channel for dialogue. I would personally save up more and buy the Sony model over the Amazon.

In a recent development, but if I were to save more money, I'd choose the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar (non-Plus) over the Plus version. Sure, there's no subwoofer, but it's just $119 and genuinely sounds fantastic. It's the best budget soundbar I've ever tested.

Hmm. This is a tricky one. I loved the basic Amazon Fire TV Soundbar — if you want seriously great sound at a low price, get that one. The extra $130 for the Plus model? Not worth it, if you ask me. I would either spend an extra $50 on the Samsung B750F or an extra $130 on the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, due to a lack of communication between the built-in subwoofer and the main channel speakers, dialogue can be overpowered during action-heavy scenes. Consequently, I can’t recommend this model over the Samung B750F. Personally, I would either get the cheaper Amazon Fire TV Soundbar or the aforementioned Samsung model. Or, you could save up a little extra for the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer ($375) or the with Rears version ($489).

However, if you have an Amazon Fire TV and want something capable of integrating into the ecosystem seamlessly (even though you'll need a separate Fire stick or Fire TV), without having to spend an extra $50 on the B750F, the Plus is a great deal.

Apple TV+’s Presumed Innocent will be back for a second season, but Season 2 will diverge from the first installment.

Recent findings suggest that the legal drama series was renewed in July 2024 with its final two episodes still to launch on Apple TV+. Starting out as a limited series, the series will take on an anthology style like The White Lotus after becoming Apple’s most-watched show.

Read on for all the plot details, character casting and more about Presumed Innocent Season 2.

In a recent development, when will Presumed Innocent Season 2 come out? Watch on Deadline.

In November, Apple unveiled that the second season of the crime drama will premiere February 19, 2027 with its first two episodes. The rest will follow weekly through April 2.

Who will be in the cast of Presumed Innocent Season 2?

Rachel Brosnahan (The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, Superman) will lead Season 2 of the legal series alongside Jack Reynor (Midsommar, The Perfect Couple, whose casting Deadline reported exclusively. Matthew Rhys (The Americans, Perry Mason)was also cast as a lead in early September 2025, and Fiona Shaw (Bad Sisters, Killing Eve) was cast as a series regular Oct. 1. Still more names include Courtney B. Vance, John Magaro, Michael Hsu Rosen and Lesley-Ann Brandt.

Ji-young Yoo (KPop Demonhunters, Expats) will recur in Season 2 as Deadline revealed in January 2026.

According to recent reports, what happened in Presumed Innocent Season 1? Who was in the cast of Presumed Innocent Season 1?

Season 1 of the series was inspired by Scott Turow’s 1987 courtroom thriller novel of the same name. It starred Jake Gyllenhaal in the main role of Rusty Sabich, the character Harrison Ford played in the 1990 film adaptation of Turow’s best-seller.

The cast of Season 1 also included Bill Camp as Raymond Horgan, Renate Reinsve as Carolyn Polhemus, Ruth Negga as Barbara Sabich, O-T Fagbenle as Nico Della Guardia, Peter Sarsgaard as Tommy Molto, Elizabeth Marvel as Lorraine Horgan, Lily Rabe as Dr. Liz Rush, Chase Infiniti as Jaden Sabich and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw launched Moonlock on the Mac, the company described its upcoming app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Users can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that shows where apps are sending data and lets users block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the manufacturer indicates “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping users improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets users swiftly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

According to recent reports, as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, customers can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

“When we debuted Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

#74336. Clojure will affect the way you think about programming (2017)

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1240 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegreenplace ↗ Open Full Page

Clojure will affect the way you think about programming (2017)

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1240 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegreenplace

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I sometimes get asked for recommendations of what programming language to "learn next".
  • According to recent reports, in this post I want to explain why I think Clojure is a terrific language for this task.
  • First and foremost, Clojure belongs to the Lisp family of languages, like Common Lisp, Scheme and Racket.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I sometimes get asked for recommendations of what programming language to "learn next". It's great that folks appreciate the fact that being exposed to several sufficiently different programming languages is an key step on the path to programming enlightenment. But it's also true that, given limited free time, the choice of which languages to learn is important. As the famous quote by Alan Perlis indicates:.

According to recent reports, in this post I want to explain why I think Clojure is a terrific language for this task. Whatever your background, it's almost guaranteed to affect the way you think about programming. It's a fairly newly introduced language (from 2007) that did a good job of collecting insights and paradigms from many existing languages and organizing them into a coherent whole. It's chock-full of great ideas. In other words, the perfect language to expand your brain.

First and foremost, Clojure belongs to the Lisp family of languages, like Common Lisp, Scheme and Racket. Lisp is one of the oldest and still most crucial families of programming languages to be familiar with. Being a Lisp in this case means several things:.

It has been revealed that importantly, Clojure is a very modern Lisp, with tons of libraries for tasks common in our day and age. It also builds upon important recent research in data structures, such as efficient persistent vectors, that only appeared in the 1990s or later. I've been dabbling with various Lisps for almost 15 years, and Clojure is the first Lisp I'd consider using in production.

Recent findings suggest that I want the stress the importance of full Lisp-style macros once again. Lisp's (and Clojure's) uniform syntax and macros force us to think about the Meta-circular abstraction - there's just no way around it! We have to think of our code as data, and this has profound implications. Back in 2005, when I was still a programming neophyte, I faced a performance challenge for a data-decoding program I was hacking on in Perl. Having learned some Lisp, I had the insight of generating and evaluating new Perl code on the fly, which turned out to be key to the success of that program. I'm confident I could not have come up with that solution back then without being aware of the "Lisp way".

The designers of Clojure are extremely pragmatic, building upon decades of industry experience. I strongly recommend watching some YouTube videos of talks by leading Clojure developers. In particular, watch a few of the more popular talks by Rich Hickey - Clojure's original designer. The Alan Perlis quote mentioned above may be his most popular, but there's another I find at least as insightful:.

Sources indicate that there's a certain quality in programmers I believe we can all recognize. It can only come from real, hard-won experience of building systems for many years and pondering about how to build such systems more effectively next time. Rich Hickey certainly belongs to this quality category - his talks are very insightful, and this philosophy reigns in the design and implementation of Clojure, as well as its (friendly and vibrant) community.

Applications that process and extract useful bits of information from large datasets all look alike in many programming languages, at least to some extent. What we really want in many cases is SQL-like primitives built into our languages, but this is often challenging (.NET's LINQ is one example of a successful approach).

Clojure combines pervasive sequence protocols with persistent data structures and laziness to make this kind of task natural, using only built-in tools. Here's a realistic example of a function taken from the Clojure Applied book:.

All the functions used here are built-ins, including the ->> macro. This code reads like SQL and it's efficient too. In fact, it can be made somewhat more efficient and even seamlessly parallelized using Reducers and Transducers.

The clojure.spec library provides a degree of type-safety for nested data structures. If you've ever written comments like "this maps strings to lists, where each list element is a map of ...", clojure.spec makes it more formal and verifiable. This is very useful when working with data, and is another example of where Clojure's pragmatism shines; the language is dynamic in its core, but when you need static checking - it's there, optionally (core.typed is another option for a more statically typed flavor).

Recent findings suggest that historically, Lisp programmers weren't the biggest proponents of OOP. This doesn't mean that OOP has absolutely no value in Lisp-y languages, however. Common Lisp has had CLOS for decades, and Clojure also comes with an array of OO-like features.

Recent findings suggest that that said, Clojure's flavor of OOP is particularly powerful and tends to discourage bad practices. Clojure uses "protocols", which are a kind of interfaces, and encourages thinking in terms of protocols rather than in terms of classes with inheritance hierarchies, sort of like Go. Add to that an ability to do true multiple dispatch and you have a powerful modeling tool at your fingertips.

It wouldn't be a real language of the 2000s without powerful support for concurrency and parallelism right at the core. Clojure supports this in many ways, which are interleaved.

First, it's a functional language with persistent data structures. Persistent data structures are effectively immutable, which makes them very attractive in a multi-threaded context. Clojure has a great implementation of persistent data structures even for things like vectors (which are quite challenging to implement in an efficient manner). This is a bigger deal than may originally appear. Pure functions are often great in theory but fail in practice due to too much copying of non-trivial data structures; Clojure's elegant usage of persistent data structures solves this problem, making pure functions efficient and thus much more applicable to a wide array of problems.

Second, Clojure doesn't lock itself in the closet of purism and does support lower-level primitives for concurrency and mutation, where needed. Atoms are built-in mutable state units with atomic updates. Refs and transactions go further, implementing STM.

Third, Clojure comes with a bunch of concurrency tools built in. Promises, futures and threads leverage the underlying JVM's threading utilities.

Finally, Clojure has a pretty good implementation of Go's CSP in the core.async module. It provides two useful things:.

Finally, it's crucial to mention that Clojure is far from being an academic exercise. It's used in production by several companies, and has strong roots in the massive Java ecosystem. Clojure's interoperability with Java is seamless - Java code can be called from Clojure with no special provisions, and all core Clojure entities are Java objects deep under the hood.

Industry observers note that on the client side, Clojurescript has been gaining traction recently as another language-compiled-to-JS option. It brings the elegance of Clojure to client-side programming, among with some unique features like core.async for callback-free concurrency.

This doesn't mean that you should only consider Clojure as a fit for your next project. On the contrary, I recommend learning if even if there's little chance of using it in production any time soon. In fact, this was exactly my situation, Clojure is a great language to expand your programming horizons; who knows, maybe in the future you'll find it useful for some real work. If you do, great! If you don't, learning it will positively affect how you use other programming languages.

After Grand Theft Auto VI and James Bond took over social media this week, Bill Maher has added his two cents to the discourse before going on hiatus.

On Friday’s Season 24 finale of Real Time, the comedian expressed his fascination with the “giant cultural phenomenon” following GTA VI‘s multi-billion dollar opening. “No movie ever did that,” he noted.

“Grand Theft Auto came out yesterday, and about a fifth of the young men in America stayed home and didn’t go to work, to play a game,” said Maher in his opening monologue. “This thing has caused more workplace absences than ICE.”.

Thursday marked the release of Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games, the first GTA installment since 2013. Following a record-breaking launch, the highly-anticipated video game has already amassed $3.79B in its first 48 hours. Watch on Deadline.

Later in the episode, Maher said, “I am intrigued by it. But again, you are criminals, and you’re doing criminal activities—not all criminal activities, and not unmotivated criminal activities. But it is something disturbing about so many people wanting to do this.

In a recent development, “I heard … you can either choose to be a good boyfriend or a bad boyfriend,” he added. “And the guy said, ‘Why would you choose in a video game to be a good boyfriend?’ You know, people wanna smack the hooker with the car antenna. There’s just something a little disturbing about it.”.

Pivoting to Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve’s 007, Maher praised Amazon MGM Studios for the casting choice.

“I think he’s great. I don’t understand what all this hoopla is about it,” he noted. “What, is he too millennial, he’s too gay, he’s too fake? He’s great, he’s perfect … He’s 40. Perfect! You need a grown ass man to be James Bond. James Bond’s not a boy.”.

In a recent development, maher added, “And also, I would have been happy with Black James Bond, because you can be James Bond and be Black. I wouldn’t have been happy with a woman or a lesbian James Bond, that’s a different character. James Bond is a very heterosexual male, that’s too essential to not have that be a part of James Bond.”.

In a recent development, real Time‘s Season 24 finale comes after HBO gave the show another two-season renewal earlier this year, with its Season 25 return set for Jan. 15.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.

Recent findings suggest that jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Federal prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of intentionally starting the original blaze, known as the Lachman fire. While the initial fire was swiftly suppressed, unbeknownst to firefighters and other authorities at the time, embers of it continued to burn underground. On Jan. 7, heavy winds reignited the fire, causing it to surface and spread. The ensuing Palisades fire was one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people and decimating 23,448 acres of land and nearly 7,000 structures across the Pacific Palisades region.

“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”.

“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”.

After a federal jury in June deadlocked in favor of acquittal in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June, federal prosecutors narrowed their case to charge him with the two arson-related felonies rather than the three charges in the mistrial.

Industry observers note that steve Haney, the man’s lawyer for both trials, told the Los Angeles Times that they planned to appeal Friday’s verdict. “We are disappointed in the verdict, but respect the jury process,” Haney told the publication. “After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration.” Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It has been revealed that the prosecution argued that Rinderknecht, who was working on Latest Year’s Eve as an Uber driver on Dec. 31, 2024, was angry and frustrated because he was unable to find companionship on New Year’s. According to an affidavit from an investigator for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, two of his passengers described him as “agitated and angry” that night. He allegedly drove to a Pacific Palisades trailhead, where he repeatedly listened to and watched a music video for the rap song, “Un Zder, Un Thé,” about despair, and tried calling an old friend, but was unable to connect with them.Prosecutors noted that Rinderknecht started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, and that around 12:12 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman fire had begun. They said that Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of range. By the time he finally connected with the police, the fire had already been reported by others in the neighborhood.

During his call with police, per the affidavit, Rinderknecht also allegedly typed a question into ChatGPT: “Are you at fault if a fire is lift [sic] because of your cigarette?” ChatGPT allegedly responded “Yes.”.

Aqara has announced the global launch of six latest smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the company describes as “spatial intelligence.”.

The upcoming lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization ….

All of the new products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the new products support spatial intelligence.

This enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

Industry observers note that its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

It has been revealed that you might initially struggle to spot the newly introduced products in the manufacturer’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

Pricing ranges from $24 for fresh light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that yesterday, I was debugging a performance problem with our Google Forms addon. It turned out my colleague had vibe coded the logging part, so that he could monitor the newly introduced installs every week. Monitoring new customers is the most key part of running a business, so he is absolutely right in doing that. Except, he was logging the user’s email and Google has severely restricted how much detail you can get about the user since last December. So, AI had written a series of try/catch statements:.

It has been revealed that in our case, the right fix is simple. Log the timestamp, show the welcome screen first and tell marketing what they can’t get on install. But AI will never make that call for you, because it doesn’t know your customers and it won’t push back on your requirements. That is the architect’s job. If you are a developer, the coding job is going away. But it doesn’t mean your job is going away. Non-developers who don’t understand architecture and design will end up with bad performance and unmaintainable database tables. So, stop missing the coding and become an architect. Learn to push back on requirements, design the datamodel, constrain AI to it and review the code the way an architect reviews a developer’s code. You got promoted. Nobody told you, so I am telling you.

Mani - could adopting a method like spec-driven development have helped here ?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL introduced on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial patch.

Sources indicate that on Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

It has been revealed that colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a recent development, in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.
  • A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.

A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.

Ferguson, who retired in 2013, won 38 major honours during a trophy-laden 26 years at Old Trafford.

And as the 84-year-old received plaudits across the footballing world, he enjoyed a celebratory intimate setting with some of his former players and actor James Nesbitt in Manchester.

Diehard United fan Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside Michael Carrick, Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea.

In a recent development, but what are those former United players up to now? Daily Mail Sport takes a look...

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt (centre right) posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez.

Unless you've been on another planet, then you would know everything about Carrick this past week.

The 45-year-old was sacked as United head coach on Thursday morning after a disastrous start to the season.

Carrick, who has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, oversaw United's worst top-flight start since Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 Premier League matches as they sit 18th.

Furthermore this season, he only won three of 15 games in all competitions.

Industry observers note that the downturn in the Red Devils' form is bewildering considering their upturn when Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January last season. He was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday morning by club chiefs.

He oversaw United's worst top-flight start in Premier League history with one win in 10 games.

Like Carrick, Evans is also out of a job having been part of his backroom staff at United as first-team coach.

After retiring as a player at the end of the 2024-25 season, Evans took up the position of head of loans and pathways at Carrington but left that role last December.

Following Amorim's sacking he returned to the club to help Fletcher during his caretaker manager stint before being kept on by Carrick.

Like Carrick, Evans was relieved of his United duties having been part of his backroom team.

The sole former player still connected directly with the club, Fletcher is their Under 18s head coach. The Scot had to pause his role last season when becoming the club's first-team interim head coach following Amorim's sacking in January - drawing 2-2 with Burnley in the Premier League before overseeing their FA Cup third-round home defeat by Brighton a few days later.

Having come through the club's academy, Fletcher knows what it takes to make the grade at the club and has the likes of Kai Rooney, son of Wayne, and Jacey Carrick, son of Michael, among his squad.

And Fletcher's young charges are enjoying a strong start to the season which has included six goals in wins over Liverpool (6-3) and Burnley (6-0) at the end of last month.

Fletcher is the Red Devils' U18s head coach - nurturing the club's latest crop of rising stars.

The former Red Devils captain had ambitions to go into coaching, having done his badges, but has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio - telling Gary Neville on The Overlap last July that he had put £4.5million into building 76 one or two-bedroom apartments in Belgrade, Serbia.

However, this summer it was reported that Vidic had been a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

According to Serbian media, encrypted messages show then-Serbia's football president Slavisa Kokeza wanted people to threaten Vidic after he had publicly criticised the Serbian Football Association (FSS) over the national side's failure to qualify for the Euro 2020 tournament.

In the reported devised plot in 2020, Kokeza reportedly told one contact to make it clear to Vidic that he should 'stay away from the association or he will end up in a ditch'.

As well as that, criminals were hired to monitor the former centre-back's movements in Milan, where he lived, and fit his car with a tracking device.

Following the revelations, Vidic and his legal team filed a criminal complaint and sought an investigation into the claimed plot.

'In mid-May, OCCRP and KRIK visited my home and told me they had obtained encrypted messages from Sky ECC (a now-defunct communication encryption service which EUROPOL said was widely used by criminals and was broken into by European police in 2021) and analysed them,' Vidic told The Athletic in July.

'The messages were said to have come from the then-president of the SFF in 2020. They were about me and how to stop me from talking to the media. At the time, I was commentating on the situation in Serbian football. I was living in Milan, Italy, where I stayed after finishing my career with Inter. I hadn't yet moved back to Serbia, where I am from and where I live.'.

Vidic, who has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio, was reportedly a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

Van der Sar's calm persona on the football pitch translated well into the boardroom during his near-seven-year stint at Ajax as their chief executive officer.

The former Manchester United goalkeeper joined the Dutch giants' board in 2012, becoming CEO in 2016. During his spell Ajax reached the 2017 Europa League final and 2019 Champions League semi-finals with a young exciting core of players including the likes of Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt.

The year Van der Sar left though Ajax finished third that season to qualify for the Europa League play-offs, missing out on the Champions League for the first time since 2009.

A few weeks later in July 2023, Van der Sar was put in intensive care after suffering a brain haemorrhage while on holiday in Croatia.

Three years on since recovering, Van der Sar is enjoying being away from football for the time being telling The Overlap in February: 'Now it's almost three years ago, so I've had time to recover with no stress, no phone in my hand - just doing the stuff that I've wanted to do.

Industry observers note that 'Wake up when you want, walk the dog, go swim in the sea, go on holiday. I went to New Zealand for two months with [wife] Annemarie - nice things that I never had the chance to do before.

'I started playing at 18 or 19, finished at 40, and at 41 I became one of the directors at Ajax until 53, so I thought it was the right time to take a step back. That's taken a little bit longer than I originally thought, to be fair, but we are enjoying ourselves very much.'.

Van der Sar was Ajax CEO for seven years before stepping down from the role in 2023.

The ex-goalkeeper is now enjoying life with wife Annemarie after a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

Like Carrick, Van Persie has turned his hand to first-team management since retiring.

According to recent reports, his first role was with Dutch outfit Heerenveen - signing a two-year contract with the club ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, his time there lasted just nine months as he took over the reins at Dutch giants Feyenoord.

However, his time in Rotterdam lasted just 16 months there when he was sacked in June. He had guided them to second in the Eredivisie but they finished 19 points behind champions PSV Eindhoven.

In explaining his sacking, newly-appointed technical director Devy Rigaux cited the style of play as a factor.

'We conducted a thorough internal analysis,' he noted. 'In this, we took into account, among other things, the development of the style of play and the declining trend in terms of points total, both in Europe and in the Eredivisie.

'The conclusion was that it is better to start the next season with a newly introduced head coach.'.

The 43-year-old is awaiting a fresh job, like Carrick.

Van Persie is presently without a managerial job after being sacked by Feyenoord in June.

The sole player from this list to still be playing, Hernandez made history by becoming the first-ever player signed to USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas.

In July, the 38-year-old penned a two-year deal with an option for a third year at the expansion club which will play in the second-tier of US football, below Major League Soccer.

The Mexican striker still has a few months to wait for his debut though, with the season not beginning until March 2027.

In the meantime, he was part of the FOX broadcast team for the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, serving as an analyst.

Last year, Hernandez was caught up in a sexism storm, which he later apologised for, after he made a series of statements on TikTok 'promoting sexist stereotypes that are considered media violence and go against gender equality in sport'.

Hernandez stated women are 'failing' and 'eradicating masculinity'.

'Don't be afraid to be women, to allow yourselves to be led by a man,' said the former Mexico captain on social media.

His remarks sparked a backlash, which led to his apology which included him saying: 'I deeply regret any confusion or discomfort that my recent words have caused.'.

Hernandez was fined and warned about his future conduct.

Hernandez, who attended United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, is the only player still playing and has signed for USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas ahead of their fresh term.

Like the majority of the names here, O'Shea's post-playing career has seen him turn to coaching with his current role being the Republic of Ireland assistant head coach.

The 45-year-old has been in this position since August 2024, staying on with his homeland's setup following the appointment of Heimir Hallgrimsson as manager.

It has been revealed that O'Shea took charge of the team for four friendly fixtures that year following Stephen Kenny's departure in November 2023. His record read one win, one draw and two defeats in that period.

The former defender will be hoping to help his country qualify for Euro 2028 which will be played on home soil across the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales.

O'Shea is Republic of Ireland assistant head coach - a role he has held since August 2024.

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of latest devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

We’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report says the bezels are around 1mm thick.

The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.

ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ricapar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It runs on an IBM PC XT: an 8088 at 4.77 MHz, 640K of RAM, a CGA card.
  • Backstory: The IBM PC was my first computer.
  • It was already obsolete by the time I was old enough to use it, but at 5 years old it was a magical device that I could make do different things depending on what I typed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An AI coding agent for DOS. It runs on an IBM PC XT: an 8088 at 4.77 MHz, 640K of RAM, a CGA card.

Backstory: The IBM PC was my first computer. Rather, it was my parents’ first personal computer that I got to use at a very early age.

It was already obsolete by the time I was old enough to use it, but at 5 years old it was a magical device that I could make do different things depending on what I typed.

I learned how to type and use DOS so that I could launch some early “Learn the Alphabet” games that my mom had bought me. I learned some elementary-level use of BASIC, but at the time that didn’t progress much further than making some number guessing games and other small projects.

Sources indicate that from there, many years passed but I still have some of the original parts of that PC. I have a collection of vintage machines that mean something to me, with my fully maxed-out IBM PC 5160 being the centerpiece of my collection. It still has a working 20 MB hard drive, but that’s disconnected in favor of a PicoMEM that lets me emulate a hard drive off of an SD card, making experimentation and play much easier.

Industry observers note that old, meet upcoming. New, meet old: I love intersections of old and new technology. What better way to cross the two than building an AI coding agent to run on DOS on original hardware?

And of course, what better to build it than an AI coding agent?

I (read: Claude) built this for my own entertainment. I wanted to see how far I could push an AI coding agent to build something given out of the (modern) norm of constraints. Also, can that something it built then build other somethings? 100% of this repo is written by Claude, with the exception of the text within this box.

As explained in more detail below, the harness runs on the native OS and hardware and relies on a “bridge” PC in order to handle TLS, which would’ve been more than what an 8088 could handle.

Type CLAWDOS at the C:\> prompt and talk to Claude. It reads and edits the files on your disk, writes programs, compiles them with Turbo C, runs them and looks at what they draw on the screen. It keeps notes between conversations and picks up where it left off.

The whole harness runs on the PC. HARNESS.EXE is a 176 KB DOS program that speaks the Claude Messages API itself: it writes the requests, parses the streamed reply, runs the tools and keeps every conversation on its own disk. The 8088 does everything but TLS.

Every screen below comes from a 5160 at 4.77 MHz, emulated in 86Box. The conversations are with the live API.

One message: “Write PRIMES.C: print the primes below 100. Compile it with Turbo C and run it.” ClawDOS reads its guide to the compilers on this machine, writes the source, then compiles, links and runs it in a single tool call. The answer is on the screen 64 seconds after Enter, 26 of them spent compiling, linking and running.

In a recent development, the compiler gets the machine to itself. For a build, ClawDOS saves its state and leaves memory, Turbo C runs with about 450K free, and the harness comes back on the same conversation with the program’s output in hand.

Recent findings suggest that clawDOS wrote this tribute to the 1983 film on the PC itself: a vector world map, missiles arcing over the pole, a tic-tac-toe endgame, and a score for the PC speaker or an AdLib card. Five files of Turbo C, 15 KB of source, a WG.EXE under 10 KB.

Here it is running on the real 5160, filmed off its IBM monitor:.

▶ Watch the WarGames demo on YouTube.

According to recent reports, start a latest conversation and “your WarGames demo” is all it needs. ClawDOS opens the note it saved in C:\MEMORY, finds the latest build, and recalls the palette trick the war scene plays on the CGA.

That Run call asked for a screenshot 25 seconds in. A timer-interrupt hook copies the CGA’s video memory at that moment, the 8088 encodes it as a PNG, and the picture goes to Claude with the tool result. This is the file the PC made, 320x200 in four colours, 16 KB:.

And this is what Claude made of it:.

It has been revealed that asked to make the demo exit on its own, ClawDOS goes looking. It searches the sources for the keyboard wait, reads the file, says what it found and edits one line. Each tool call shows in the transcript with its result, and between them Claude says what it is about to do.

Text art in sixteen colours, straight into the transcript, and music on the PC speaker in GW-BASIC’s PLAY language.

According to recent reports, A chat screen built for the CGA. Replies stream onto the screen as they arrive, word-wrapped at 80 columns in code page 437. Writes are timed to the retrace, so there is no snow. The transcript scrolls in hardware through the CRTC start address, with PgUp and PgDn to go back. The spinner and its seconds run from the timer interrupt and keep moving while the PC is busy.

Recent findings suggest that eighteen tools. Claude works on the machine through these:.

A development kit on the disk. Two assemblers (TINYASM and WASM), Bruce’s C, GW-BASIC and the lDebug debugger, plus Turbo C 2.0, installed from your own floppy images in external/. All of them are proven on the 8088, and ClawDOS knows how to drive each one.

In a recent development, memories and skills. Memories are what ClawDOS learns on your PC: what you built together, what worked, what you like. Skills are guides that ship with it, such as the dev tools and CGA demo effects. Both are plain text files on the disk, listed in every conversation’s system prompt and read when they fit the task. F4 browses the memories:.

Sources indicate that safe mode. On by default. Anything that changes a file, memory or a port asks Allow ...? (y/n) first. F3 turns it off.

Conversations that last. Every chat is a file on the disk in the API’s own message format. F6 lists them, Enter reopens one, and your next message carries it on. A chat cut off by the power switch reopens too.

In a recent development, any model, mid-conversation. /model lists the providers in CLAWDOS.CFG and switches between them and their models without losing the conversation. F5 sets how hard Claude thinks, from low to max. Any host that speaks the Messages API works.

Industry observers note that easy on a slow link. The system prompt and tools are cached by the API. After a conversation’s first request the PC uploads only what is newly introduced, so a tool result goes up in about 500 bytes. A dropped connection or an overloaded API is retried, and the turn carries on.

A flight recorder. CLAWDOS.LOG has a line for every round: time to first token, upload size and time, tokens in and out, cache reads.

docs/API.md has exactly what ClawDOS sends and what it expects back.

You need a Mac or a Windows PC with Python 3, and an Anthropic API key. On Windows the command is python.

At the C:\> prompt, type CLAWDOS.

According to recent reports, no key? python3 tunnel/mockapi.py plays the API offline: type CLAWDOS 10.0.2.2:18023 and send !help.

On a real PC: build with the address of the machine running the tunnel (python3 scripts/build.py --tunnel 192.168.1.10:8443), copy CLAWDOS.IMG to the PicoMEM’s microSD card, pick it as the hard disk in the PicoMEM’s menu, boot, and type CLAWDOS. Later builds update the card’s image in place and keep its memories and chats (python3 scripts/build.py --update /path/to/CLAWDOS.IMG).

/model, /chats, /memories, /latest and /quit work from the input box. CLAWDOS -m "..." sends a message from the command line and -c NAME reopens a chat.

Sources indicate that clawDOS is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version: see LICENSE. HARNESS.EXE links mTCP, which is GPLv3. The FreeDOS boot sector in src/boot/freedos is vendored unmodified under its own GPLv2-or-later license (its COPYING). Disk images you build hold other people’s software (FreeDOS, mTCP, and Turbo C from your own floppies): don’t redistribute an image with Turbo C on it.

ClawDOS stands on mTCP, FreeDOS, Open Watcom, the PicoMEM, 86Box and DOSBox-X.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syrian actor Taim Hasan (Al Haybar) has signed to star in Neon-backed biopic Caesar, about military officer Farid Al-Madhhan who risked his life to expose torture and human-rights abuses in prisons under Bashar Al Assad’s reign as president.

At the same time, Ameer Fakher Eldin has been unveiled as the director on the drama. The Ukraine-born, Germany-based Syrian Lebanese filmmaker is known for films including Yunan and The Stranger.

Sources indicate that hasan has a substantial following across the Middle East and North Africa where he has built a career in Syrian, Lebanese and Egyptian productions, with notable recent roles including Jabal in hit organized crime drama Al Hayba and Mawlana. Related Stories News Steven Paul Talks Up Federal Film & TV Tax Credit: "It's Going To Be Good For The World" - Industry Days Doha News Candle Media's Kevin Mayer Says Firm Caught Out By Drop In Streamer Demand: "We Didn't See That Contraction Coming".

Sources indicate that the signings were announced at a press conference at the Film Committee at Media City Qatar’s second Industry Days Doha, taking place within the framework of the Doha Film Festival, with Al-Madhhan, Hasan and Eldin in attendance. Mike Larocca, co-founder of Department M, a key partner on the project, also joined the presentation. Watch on Deadline.

“The story of Caesar is not simply a story of suffering. It is not just the story of a photographer or someone who took pictures. It is a story about humanity. It is a story about confronting challenges. Above all, it is an ethical story. That is what we have worked to communicate,” stated Al-Madhlan.

Industry observers note that “This was never intended to be simply a forensic or documentary exercise. It is a human story – the story of people who had lives, families and experiences, but whose lives unfortunately ended in inhumane circumstances.”.

The project was first declared at the first edition of the Industry Days Doha in 2025, with the Film Committee revealing it had acquired the life rights to al-Madhhan’s story and was partnering with Department M, Kuwait’s Sard Media Group and Doha-based Katara Studios on the planned feature with Neon on board as a distributor.

The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights documented more than 650,000 deaths in Syria’s civil war, which began in 2011, with an estimated 60,000 people believed to have died from torture in detention centers.

Al-Madhhan was the Head of the Forensic Evidence Department of the Military Police in Damascus before fleeing Syria in 2014 with more than 54,000 images for the human rights abuses taking place in the country’s prisons.

He spent three years smuggling evidence out via hidden memory cards inside his clothes and loaves of bread. Fearing for his life, he hid behind the pseudonym of Caesar only to unveil his true identity last year in the wake of Al Assad’s ousting in December 2024.

It has been revealed that the images he gathered were used to raise awareness around the brutality of the Al-Assad regime. His evidence also informed the bipartisan 2019 Caesar Act in the U.S., introducing sanctions targeting Al-Assad and his collaborators.

Industry observers note that “This project carries a tremendous responsibility,” said Hasan. “It is about the collective conscience of a nation and the individual experiences of people in Syria. I would particularly like to thank the team for approaching the story with such bravery and respect.”.

In a recent development, “We will tackle this project with the utmost care and sensitivity, working closely with my partners, Michael and everyone contributing to its success. As much as we want to portray the many different dimensions of Caesar’s story, we also want to show the beauty of Syria and the bravery of its people. We want to portray the real Syria,” he said.

According to recent reports, the Caesar signings are among a raft of announcements made by the Film Committee across the Industry Days, running from November 19 to 21 within the framework of the Doha Film Festival. Hasan received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the opening night of the festival.

Never Lend Money, Pay Your F-cking Taxes, and More Life Advice From Leslie Jones

💡 Key Takeaways
  • T here’s not a room in the world that could fit all of the trinkets, gifts, and prized possessions comedian Leslie Jones has accumulated through her career.
  • Industry observers note that “I always keep something,” Jones states on Zoom from her Los Angeles home, panning the camera to show a wall of white shelves packed to the brim with tchotchkes.
  • Jones might be one of the best-known late-bloomers in show business.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

T here’s not a room in the world that could fit all of the trinkets, gifts, and prized possessions comedian Leslie Jones has accumulated through her career.

Industry observers note that “I always keep something,” Jones states on Zoom from her Los Angeles home, panning the camera to show a wall of white shelves packed to the brim with tchotchkes. But it’s hard for her to pick favorites — especially since they all have treasured memories that go along with them. “Colin [Jost] gave me a trophy that noted ‘Baddest Bitch in the World,’” she says with a laugh, pointing at the memento. “I’ve still got that one.”.

Jones might be one of the best-known late-bloomers in show business. In 2014, she joined Saturday Night Live as a writer before being promoted to a featured player. She was 47 at the time, making her the oldest person ever to join the cast. But even with two decades of stand-up work under her belt, slogging through bombed sets, late-night performances, and side hustles, Jones indicates she doesn’t regret her winding path to comedy fame. In fact, she’s adamant that if success had happened for her any sooner, she wouldn’t be here to talking to us. “I would have been a cautionary tale,” she says, plainly. “I would have made all the wrong decisions.”.

Jones spent five seasons on SNL, where she established herself as a comedic voice known for taking wild — and often foul-mouthed — swings at everything from dating during slavery to abortion bans to plans for her own funeral. This brash self-assuredness followed her even after her tenure, as she expanded her résumé to include TV and film roles in projects like Ghostbusters and Coming 2 America as well as professional fan duties — Chief Super Fan Commentator, to be precise — for NBC’s Olympics broadcasts. From her New York Times-bestselling memoir Leslie Fcking Jones to her latest gig hosting HGTV’s Roast My Rental (which debuted over the summer and re-airs through the end of November, and can be streamed on HBO Max), Jones has cemented herself as an outspoken and hilarious presence in pretty much any medium. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It has been revealed that “I’m making it work,” she says. “There’s no such thing as not waking up and getting some shit done.”.

For Rolling Stone’s Last Word column, Jones talked through nearly blowing off her SNL audition, vacation horror stories, and how to end the political divide in America.

Sources indicate that what was your first job as a teenager?Damn, that took me way back. I worked at this place called Lounge Car Tours. My mom worked in accounting or something and she got me a job cleaning the buses. She tried to teach me how to drive her car, which was a stick, and I ran into one of the buses.

It has been revealed that when did you realize comedy was for you? The first time I touched the mic. In college [at Colorado State University], I did the “funniest person on campus” contest. Whoever won got to open up for the comedians that were coming into town. When I was at that contest, I [felt] like, “Oh, I’ve already been doing this 10 years.”.

Sources indicate that what’s the worst experience you’ve had bombing at a show?It was six months into me performing. This dude in the audience started heckling. I bombed and then I went back the next week. He was there, he didn’t say a word, and I still bombed.

According to recent reports, how do you handle hecklers now? I tear they ass up. It depends on what type of heckler it is. If it’s a nice heckler, I’ll do something fun. But if it’s a mean or rude heckler, I try to make them feel like they’ll never speak again in public.

In a recent development, what’s something you wish you had known early in your career?I don’t think I would have wanted to know, because I like that I learned my way. Maybe not to just make friends so easily. Don’t trust so easily. What was the first big purchase that you made with your comedy money?Don’t laugh. I bought this Michael Kors purse. It was $300. I thought I was the shit. Then my friend was like, “Bitch, that’s just a Michael Kors purse. That’s not no Louis [Vuitton]. The fuck is wrong with you?”.

According to recent reports, how does it feel in your body when you get a laugh from an audience?Like a high. Adrenaline. It’s a great feeling — ticklish.

What’s the best advice you’ve ever gotten? November of ’87, I performed at this place called the World Comedy Club [in Times Square]. This comedian named Speedy had a show. Speedy’s best friends with Jamie Foxx, so Jamie came to close the show for him. I did that show. Did terrible. Bombed. I remember watching Jamie perform, going, “I got to figure out how he does this.” I had him in the corner like, “How do I become a better comic?” He was like, “How old are you?” I was 19. He was like, “You’re a baby. You don’t know anything. You don’t have no jokes. Go and live your life. Get your heart broken. Break hearts. Get fired. Get hired. Go live a life so you can have something to talk about.”.

Did you take the advice? Yeah. I was working. I was never trying to get a job to try to find myself — I was always trying to get a job to make money. I think young people have that equation wrong. I worked at Denny’s and then I sold perfume in the parking lot. I worked at the justice of the peace for a little, then the post office. Then I waitressed at Spoons [Grill & Bar, in Orange County]. I think I waited on [SNL cast member] Mikey Day while I was there. He used to go there all the time! I feel like I waited on him because [once I got to SNL], he had an obsession with me with his sketches. He would write sketches every time where I was either yelling at him or beating him up. I was like, “Mikey, do you want me to beat you up? Is this a thing you have?”.

Sources indicate that what’s your strongest memory from your SNL audition? Chris Rock got me the audition. He came in [to the Comedy Store in L.A.] one night, saw me perform, and then called me like two days later and was like, “Hey, I just had dinner with Lorne Michaels and he’s gonna call you for an audition for SNL.” I know he expected me to go crazy, but my brother had just died and I didn’t care about shit. When he called me, I went off on him. He said, “You’re a dumbass. Go to the fucking audition and do some jokes” and hung up. I called my manager livid — ”Fucking Chris Rock got me a fucking audition for SNL. How dare he?” My manager was like, “OK, I’m gonna need you to take a second to shut the fuck up. Have you lost your mind? Leslie, if you don’t go to that audition, I will quit.” I go to the Comedy Store just knowing I’m gonna find somebody that’s going to agree with me. And every comedian up there was looking at me like [I was] the dumbest motherfucker.

We know how it ended — you were on the show for five seasons — but how did you spin that attitude in the room with Lorne?I was like, “You know what? I’m a go, so I can show them that I don’t need this shit.” Oh, God, the arrogance! By the end of that week, I wanted that job. I was so wrong. “There’s so much shit I can learn here.”.

Recent findings suggest that I remember being in Indianapolis on the phone with my manager, and my manager was like, “Yeah, I think they’re gonna go with someone else, homie.” And I was like, “Yeah, I think so, too.” I was depressed. I was like, “Fuck. Do I take this job that my aunt is offering me? Because if I keep doing this, I ain’t gonna have no retirement money. I ain’t gonna be able to take care of myself when I get older. I’m 47 already, so maybe I should just go on back to Memphis and she can get me a job.” Then they called me.

According to recent reports, how did you decide it was time to leave SNL?People try to act like they don’t know when they’re supposed to leave a situation. You know when you’re supposed to leave your job. You know when it’s time to move to the next level. If I was there when I was in my twenties, I would have stayed a long, long time just because I needed to learn and make money and get the connections. But [Lorne] got me when I was 47. And after five years of being there, I wasn’t ready to settle for that being my job the rest of my life. So it was, “If I don’t leave right now, I won’t be able to leave.”.

It has been revealed that during the 2024 Paris Olympics, you were NBC’s Chief Super Fan Commentator. Are there any Olympic sports you feel you could make a solid attempt at?Oh, hell, no! Nah. The Olympics is the best of the best. There’s nothing I could do — maybe [jumping] around with the little ribbon.

Recent findings suggest that on HGTV’s Roast My Rental, you help people fix up short-term homes. Do you have any of your own vacation-home or rental horror stories?Oh, yeah! I stayed in a place where they had a beehive in the wall. Then he had the nerve to say “Those bees wasn’t there before you got there.” Oh, so I brought the hive and climbed down a mountain, scaled up on the wall, and stuck that beehive right behind the bed? Yeah, that’s what I did.

In a recent development, who are some people who’ve encouraged or supported you through your career? When I met them, they gave me great advice: Whoopi Goldberg, Arsenio Hall, Damon Wayans. Bill Bellamy, Greg Fitzsimmons. So many comedians.

How do you approach romantic relationships?What is that? A candy bar? That’s why I’m single now. I don’t approach them. I burn them down. I don’t know. You tell me.

Is there an album that corresponds to meaningful or transformative times in your life?Stevie Wonder, Talking Book. It has “Visions,” one of the best songs ever written. It’s the most beautiful, beautiful song. Stevie Wonder and Donny Hathaway are very important to me. I love music. My dad loved music. For a long time, he thought I was gonna be a musician because I knew music so well, just like he knew it. That’s back in the day when people used to write songs, write poetry. Now it’s just about how fast they can get into somebody’s drawers.

Are there any projects you’ve turned down that you wish you’d noted yes to?No. There’s projects that I said yes to that I wish I said no to.

Industry observers note that what are some of those?I ain’t gonna mention them. My publicist will be like, “God dammit, Leslie!”.

Recent findings suggest that what’s a performance you’re proudest of? All my [Weekend] Updates on SNL. And there’s a sketch I did about the Upper East Side. I really am glad I did that — that’s one of my things I love the most.

Industry observers note that what are some rules that you live by?Don’t shit where I eat — meaning don’t fuck people you work with. It’s the Number One rule because you will fuck your shit up. Don’t lend money. Just give it, because waiting on people to pay you back, you’re just gonna be frustrated. Passion at all times. Do everything with passion. Even if you’re folding your clothes. I can tell a person’s character just by how they fold their clothes. Always be intentional and enjoy everything — don’t skip days. Don’t say, “Hey, I can’t wait until it’s Tuesday.” Enjoy the days up until Tuesday.

Do you think you could have handled fame if it had happened to you when you started comedy at 19? No, absolutely not. Oh, thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Lord, for not letting me make it at 19. When you get stuff young, you stop creating. You stop growing. It’s good for a child to grow up. No one should get things before it’s time. I’ve seen so many comedians crash because they get that stuff early. I’m glad that I went through the stuff that I went through, because when I did get famous, I knew how to handle it. I don’t think I would have been that way at 19. Oh, God, the scandals! I would have fucked everybody. I’m serious. Industry observers note that what’s your advice to people who want to get into comedy or entertainment? Don’t look at the now. Look at the how. I didn’t just pop up. There’s no such thing as an overnight success, and there’s no such thing as sacrificing everything so you can make it. If you’re trying to make it, still get a job, pay your fucking rent, pay your fucking taxes, get some goddamn health insurance, live a regular life. Don’t be a starving artist — there’s no fucking such thing. And whatever craft that you’re going into, you are not better than that craft. That craft has been there way before you, and it will be there way after you’re dead. So, don’t think that you’re better than the craft of comedy. Bow to the craft.

It has been revealed that you’re no stranger to mixing comedy and politics. What are your thoughts on America’s current political moment? I want everybody to understand that the reason that we have so much hate right now is because we don’t have love for ourselves individually. You can’t give something that you don’t have. I know that sounds like a cliché, but you have to start loving yourself. Every part — your insecurities, your badness, your mistakes, your flaws, your wonderfulness, all of that. The only way we’re gonna beat all of this hate is if everyone starts having a full, solid love for themselves. Because when you love yourself and actually like yourself, you don’t want to hurt nobody. And then you will get your ass up and go vote.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as a certified personal trainer, I work with a wide range of clients who have lots of different fitness goals. But for my clients in their 60s and beyond, there’s usually one objective that drives their training: improving balance and stability.

In a recent development, I recently started working with a 60-year-old client who wanted to focus on just that. She noticed that she was a little more unsteady on her feet than she used to be, and had a few close calls with falling. After a thorough check-up with her doctor, we began our work together with the following routine.

These exercises aren’t just for seniors. It’s never too early to start thinking about your balance, so give them a try during your next workout. They’re appropriate for any fitness level and you won’t need any equipment to do them (but adding a dumbbell or two will always make things more challenging).

Check in with your doctor before trying any newly introduced workout, especially if you have balance concerns.

According to recent reports, these exercises aren’t hard, but doing them correctly is important. Beginners should consider meeting with a personal trainer or physical therapist for feedback and guidance on form, and to get modifications if needed.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll just need some room and an elevated platform, like a stair step, for this workout. Hang onto a chair or another stable surface for additional support if you need it.

It has been revealed that start by doing each exercise for one set of 10 reps. As your balance improves, you can add an additional set and increase your reps to 12. You can also use small dumbbells for the step-up to balance to ramp up the difficulty.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

These exercises can be done on their own or as a warm-up for other activities.

You may feel muscle fatigue when doing this workout, but you should never feel sharp pain. Stop the workout immediately and consult your physician if you feel sharp pain at any point.

Here’s how to do the exercises:.

The exercises in this workout force you to find equilibrium when your center of gravity is maintained over a smaller surface area – either one foot for the standing marches, step up to balance, and side step to balance, or a narrow placement of two feet for the heel-to-toe walks.

During these exercises, your deep core muscles like the rectus abdominis and internal obliques engage to stabilize and support your entire body. Your glutes and hip stabilizing muscles also work to keep the hips in a level position. The stronger these muscles are, the more conditioned they’ll be to keep you upright and sturdy during everyday movement.

Additionally, exercises like the step-up to balance strengthen key muscle groups in your lower body, like the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.

The life and legacy of legendary Egyptian artist Mohamed Mounir is set to be explored in a biopic spearheaded by The Film Committee at Media City Qatar.

The Film Committee has acquired the rights to document Mounir’s life story, with partners on the project set to include a leading regional studio and other partners, which have yet to be unveiled.

In a recent development, the project was revealed at the Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days, just hours after the Qatari body gave an update on previously announced biopic Caesar, about Syrian whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan, announcing Taim Hasan as it star. Related Stories News 'Al Hayba' Star Taim Hasan To Play Syrian Whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan In Neon-Backed 'Caesar' Biopic News Steven Paul Talks Up Federal Film & TV Tax Credit: "It's Going To Be Good For The World" - Industry Days Doha.

Mounir’s career spans nearly five decades across music, film and television. Watch on Deadline.

His 1981 breakthrough album ‘Shababeek’ established him as one of Egypt’s most distinctive artists, with his work characterized by its fusion of Nubian folk and Arabic pop with Western genres like jazz, blues, and reggae.

He is known to his fans across the Middle East and beyond as “El King” in reference to his 1998 album and play ‘El Malek Howwa El Malek’ ((The King is The King).

Also working in cinema, his some 20 credits including collaborations with late Egyptian filmmaker Youssef Chahine on films including Egyptian Story (1982) and Destiny, which played in Out of Competition in Cannes in 1997 and was then selected as Egypt’s Oscar entry.

Industry observers note that mounir was born into a Nubian family in a village in Southern Egypt, where he spent his early childhood. His family moved to Cairo, after the village was resettled due to the construction of the Aswan Dam in the 1960s, where his singing voice was discovered when he sang at a family gathering.

The Film Committee said the biopic will trace Mounir’s journey from his humble beginnings to becoming one of the Arab world’s most celebrated and influential artists, revealing untold details, surprises, stories and anecdotes.

“Mohamed Mounir’s music holds a special place in the lives of audiences across Egypt and the Arab world,” said Film Committee at Media City Qatar Chair Hassan Al Thawadi.

“Bringing his story to the major screen is an opportunity to celebrate his artistry, the cultural heritage his work represents and its lasting social relevance, a story that connects generations of fans across the region and has the power to resonate with audiences around the world,” he continued.

“This project also builds on our recent investment in extraordinary life stories from the region and reflects our ambition to develop a world-leading slate of biographical films that brings these stories to audiences globally.”.

Alongside the feature film, aims include a behind-the-scenes documentary featuring interviews with Mounir and those who have lived and worked alongside him, as well as documenting the development and production of the biopic.

With development in the early stages, the hunt is now on for an actor to play Mounir.
